nodes.summary: Karui Mother of the Moon (the Karui sister name for the lunar goddess), involved in the myth of Ramako and Arohongui. Note: The Three Sisters page lists Lani Lua as sun and Sione as moon, contradicting the God page (Lani Lua moon, Sione sun); the wiki is inconsistent.
sources: Karui: Lani Lua (sun), Sione (moon) - wiki lists them in this order; conflicts with Karui Gods page

nodes.name: Lunaris
nodes.summary: Eternal/Azmeri moon goddess, sister of Solaris; her rivalry was engineered by Tangmazu. (PoE2 appearance of Solaris/Lunaris by name not verified in the local PoE2 corpus; Maraketh variants Solerai/Lundara and the Three Sisters myth cover PoE2.)

alt_summaries.summary: Minimal node (owned elsewhere): Sun/Moon deity of the Eternal/Templar pantheon.
Azmerian god of the Moon, sister of Solaris and Viridi, worshipped by the Eternal Empire; fought alongside Solaris at the Harbour Bridge in Act 8 after the Moon Orb is taken from Dusk.

nodes.name: The Master Below All
nodes.summary: Ancient being whose rage created the Well of Souls, power source of necromancy; nothing else known.

nodes.name: Ngamahu
nodes.summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: Halls of the Dead test; Karui tattoos by god's domain

alt_summaries.summary: Karui goddess of fire, Mother of Fire; honoured in Ngamakanui.

nodes.name: Order
nodes.summary: Impulse opposed to Chaos, representing dominion and control; Hinekora is its servant per wiki analysis; in one timeline Order overcame Chaos through Venarius's enslavement of humanity.

alt_summaries.summary: Impulse opposed to Chaos; almost nothing is known.

nodes.name: Prospero
nodes.summary: Azmerian god of wealth and the underworld, patron of the Perandus family; Cadiro struck a deal for long life.

alt_summaries.summary: Azmerian god of the underworld, patron of Cadiro.

nodes.name: Ralakesh
aliases: Ralakesh, Master of a Million Faces
nodes.summary: God of subjugation and control, Master of a Million Faces, brother of Tangmazu. Eramir says he ruled a Vaal city and enslaved Azmeri to repopulate it; the God page lists him among Azmerian/Eternal gods. His relic possessed Greust; in the Act 7 quest The Master of a Million Faces the Exile kills Greust and Sin then drains and kills Ralakesh.
sources: intro + Lore (Eramir/Sin quotes); 'Sin will then kill Ralakesh by draining its power'

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal god obsessed with control and governance; possesses Greust through a relic in Act 7 and is killed in the Forest Encampment.
Vaal god, Master of a Million Faces, who controlled a Vaal city through 'animal instincts' and nearly caused its extinction; killed by the Exile in PoE1 Act 7.

nodes.name: Ramako, Father of the Sun
nodes.summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors. claimed he was impersonated

alt_summaries.summary: Karui god of light and the sun; husband of Sione; fathered Arohongui in an alleged affair with Lani Lua, which he claims was an impostor.

nodes.name: Rongokurai, Father of the Night
nodes.summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors. whose darkness covered the visits to Sione

alt_summaries.summary: Karui god of the night; accused of helping Ramako's affair; on bad terms with Ramako.

nodes.name: Ryslatha, the Puppet Mistress
nodes.summary: Parasite-queen goddess (a carrion-insect queen covered in parasites) found in the Spawning Ground of the Wetlands. Per Sin she was once a revered matriarch whose children were slaughtered by Tukohama's warriors and who now wants to make everyone's children hers; the Azmeri believed her offspring would one day overwhelm the world. Minor Pantheon god.
sources: Sin on the Azmeri belief about Ryslatha's offspring
Act 6 dialogue "The Puppet Mistress" / "Ryslatha": tribe matriarch, children butchered by Tukohama's warriors

alt_summaries.summary: Former Azmeri matriarch who lost her children to Tukohama's warriors and became a parasitic carrion queen; Act 6 Pantheon boss.

nodes.name: Saqawal, First of the Sky
nodes.summary: Spirit Beast avatar of the First Ones, First of the Sky ('Last of the First'), ancestor of birds and reptiles; Bestiary encounter.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the named Ezomyte First Ones, god-like immortal beings of the sky; stilled the Great Fire's flames.

nodes.name: Shakari, Queen of the Sands
nodes.summary: Maraketh scorpion-goddess, daughter of Sin and Garukhan; hides in the Oasis behind a sandstorm rebuilding an ancient army and is killed in the Sand Pit (Act 9). Minor Pantheon god.
sources: Intro: daughter of Garukhan and Sin

alt_summaries.summary: Daughter of Sin and Garukhan; Queen of the Sands, twisted scorpion-like by lust for power; optional Act 9 boss.

nodes.name: Sin
nodes.summary: God, brother (twin, per the stained-glass windows) of Innocence; planted the Dark Ember beneath Highgate from which the Beast grew. In PoE1 he guides the Exile against Kitava; in PoE2 the Hooded One reveals in Act 2 that he is Sin.
sources: 'The Hooded One was likely Sin, owing to his dark appearance, apparent godhood and original planting of the Dark Ember'
intro paragraph 3 (Sin plants the Dark Ember; Beast initiates the Slumber of the Gods)
section 'Lore' (Sin captures Innocence's soul; Sin and the Exile defeat Kitava in Act 10)
Lore: reveals himself as Sin at the end of Act 2
Lore, The Beast, In-game interactions, Path of Exile 2
"I am Sin, the Forgotten One." / Act 6: "I am Sin, Thief of Virtue, and it is mine to take what I will from the defeated"
Quest log 'Speak to the Hooded One in the Shrine to the Northwest'

alt_summaries.summary: A god vilified as Sin, who planted the Dark Ember in Highgate to create the Beast and triggered the Slumber of the Gods. In PoE1 Act 10 the Exile and Sin defeat Kitava.

God, twin brother of Innocence, 'Thief of Virtue', creator of the Beast and Exile's ally in PoE1 Act 5-10 (sources the Pantheon); husband of Garukhan, father of Shakari. In PoE2 he hides as the Hooded One.
Brother of Innocence, creator of the Beast; appears to the Exile in the Chamber of Innocence and saves them from Kitava.

Thief of Virtue, twin brother of Innocence and creator of the Beast via the Dark Ember seed; in Part Two he guides the exile to harvest the souls of risen gods and Malachai's lieutenants to forge a new Dark Ember and defeat Kitava. Returns in PoE2 as 'the Hooded One'.
God Sin, 'Thief of Virtue'. In PoE2 Act 2 the Hooded One reveals himself as Sin and as the creator of the Beast.

PoE1 god, twin brother of Innocence (the stained-glass version of their tale is Templar propaganda), who planted the Dark Ember/Seed beneath Highgate to grow the Beast and lull the gods; in PoE2 he is the Hooded One (revealed in Act 2).
God who created the Beast.

nodes.name: Sione
nodes.summary: Karui Mother of the Sun, wife of Ramako, locked in endless battle with Lani Lua. See Lani Lua node for wiki inconsistency on which is sun/moon.

nodes.name: Solaris
nodes.summary: Eternal/Azmeri sun goddess, twin sister of Lunaris; led a rival cult after Tangmazu tricked her into believing Lunaris betrayed her. Sin has her soul captured for the Pantheon in Act 8. (PoE2 appearance of Solaris/Lunaris by name not verified in the local PoE2 corpus; Maraketh variants Solerai/Lundara and the Three Sisters myth cover PoE2.)

alt_summaries.summary: Minimal node (owned elsewhere): Sun/Moon deity of the Eternal/Templar pantheon.

Azmerian god of the Sun, sister of Lunaris and Viridi, recognised and worshipped by the Eternal Empire; she and Lunaris awaken in Act 8 and are summoned to the Harbour Bridge with the Sun and Moon Orbs and killed. Their flavour texts suggest a possible link to the Maraketh Sekhemas Solerai and Lundara (speculative).

nodes.name: Tangmazu
nodes.summary: Trickster god (Tekaru to the Karui, Black Crow to the Ezomytes), Ralakesh's brother, said to have made Solaris and Lunaris fight; listed on the wiki as an NPC related to Delirium and, in PoE2, revealed as the disguised Freya Hartlin whose release triggers a Delirium encounter.
sources: Freya Hartlin reveals herself as Tangmazu
Quest: Journey's End and Tangmazu reveal
Solaris, Lunaris and Viridi footnote on the Raven Trickster

alt_summaries.summary: Trickster god (Raven Trickster / Tekaru / Black Crow), brother of Ralakesh, who caused the Solaris-Lunaris feud. The Strange Voice of Delirium mirrors; in PoE2 he is bound in Kedge Bay by Karui bindings, disguised as Freya Hartlin, and freed in Dark Mists.

Trickster being imprisoned by the Ramako and later Tukohama tribes at Journey's End; disguised as Freya Hartlin, freed with Verisium Spikes, triggering a Delirium encounter. Elder Madox later calls the Raven Trickster 'he of many names and many faces' (identification only implied).

nodes.name: Tasalio
nodes.summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.

alt_summaries.summary: Karui god of water, Father of Water.

nodes.name: Tawhoa
nodes.summary: Karui Ancestor/god honoured by a Karui tribe in the Trial of the Ancestors.

alt_summaries.summary: Karui god of the forest and birds, Father of the Forest.

nodes.name: The Bodach
nodes.summary: Dark entity fought as the final boss of Legacy of the Maji after the Rite of the Nameless ('Explore the Darkness'; 'Defeat the Bodach'); the official 0.5.0 text says a prison beneath Caer Tarth holds it. At T14+ it is the Ritual pinnacle per a guide.
sources: paragraph 3: Sisters sealed away the Bodach
steps 53-54 'Explore the Darkness', 'Defeat the Bodach'; completion: Defeat The Bodach
The prison beneath it holds the Bodach

alt_summaries.summary: Embodiment of the Unlight sealed away by the Three Sisters in Wildwood Azmeri myth; PoE2 Ritual pinnacle boss in Caer Tarth, tied to the King in the Mists (0.5).

nodes.name: The Draiocht
nodes.summary: Goddess protecting the Azmeri, divided into the Three Sisters Mhacha, Catha, Morrigan who gave themselves to imbue nature; created the Wildwood and forbade gems. Original name lost.

nodes.name: The First Ones
nodes.summary: Animalistic gods worshipped by the Ezomytes, believed to roam the realm of Spirit; their avatars are Spirit Beasts: Saqawal (birds/reptiles, 'Last of the First'), Farrul (hounds/cats/mammals, 'First of the Hunt'), Fenumus (insects, 'First Explorer'), Craiceann (crabs/squid/sea life, 'First of All'). Also The Greatwolf and the Gull.
sources: Craiceann section: avatar of the First Ones

alt_summaries.summary: Group of animalistic Ezomyte gods including Craiceann, Farrul, Fenumus, Saqawal, the Greatwolf and the Gull; roam the realm of Spirit.

nodes.name: The Forgotten Daughter
nodes.summary: Unique monster in Act 2 Fellshrine Ruins representing Sin and Innocence's sister, from before the gods; presumably never ascended.

nodes.name: The Molten One
nodes.summary: Last surviving Titan from a prehistoric era, worshipped indirectly as the volcano home of the Redblade warband; writes environmental lore found in the Forge of the Titans.

alt_summaries.summary: Last known Titan from a prehistoric era, indirectly worshipped as the volcano home of the Redblade warband.

nodes.name: The Spirit
nodes.summary: Mysterious entity with which Yeena (Act 2) communicates; listed among Azmerian/Eternal gods on the God page. Nothing more is stated.

nodes.name: Tukohama
nodes.summary: Karui god of war; his tooth slashed Kitava's face. Revived by the Beast's death, he raises the Karui Fortress and is the first god the Exile captures for the Pantheon in Act 6. Kaom claimed to be his son (carvings in Kaom's Stronghold).

alt_summaries.summary: Karui god of war and minor Pantheon god; the first god the exile kills, in his Keep in the Karui Fortress. Defeating him unlocks the first Pantheon power.
Karui god of war; in the Act 4 boss fight Tavakai calls on him ('Lend me your strength') and Tukohama refuses: 'This... is not the Way.'

nodes.name: Tul, Creeping Avalanche
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords. Cold Breachlord (female per wiki). Boss residing in Tul's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).
sources: boss page: found in Hive Colony, encountered together with the other

alt_summaries.summary: Breachlord (Tul) fought as a paired boss with its counterpart in the Hive Colony (PoE2 0.5); they share a health bar in the final phase and drop the Breachlord Sac.

nodes.name: Uul-Netol, Unburdened Flesh
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords. Physical damage Breachlord. Boss residing in Uul-Netol's Domain; Breachstone/Flawless Breachstone via map device (PoE1 2.5.0; domains removed 3.28.0).

nodes.name: Vaal Oversoul
nodes.summary: Shadowy Vaal spirit entity at the top of the Ancient Pyramid; final boss of Act 2; summoned by The Apex on the Dark Altar.
sources: intro; map variant 'Vessel of the Vaal'
boss header; Shadow of the Vaal
boss header; Shadow of the Vaal
section 'Atziri's rule', Doryani's Machinarium flavour text

alt_summaries.summary: Colossal Vaal entity summoned on the Dark Altar in the Ancient Pyramid with The Apex; Act 2 final boss. Wiki gives no explicit lore on its nature; its relation to Vaal soul-worship is inferred.

Giant Vaal construct and final boss of PoE1 Act 2, fought on the top floor of the Ancient Pyramid after using The Apex on the Dark Altar; Doryani's Machinarium flavour text suggests (inference) Doryani created it. Defeating it opens the way to Act 3's Sarn.

nodes.name: Valako
nodes.summary: Karui god of storms and lightning; his jaw became a fish hook, one of Kitava's Torments.
sources: Lani: 'A fish hook that was once the Valako's Jaw'

nodes.name: Viridi
nodes.summary: Third sister of Solaris and Lunaris, Azmeri goddess of the earth, trapped within 'the orb' in Azmeri creation myth; probable namesake of the Viridian Wildwood.

nodes.name: Xesht
nodes.summary: Incomplete union of the Breachlords Xoph, Tul, Esh and Uul-Netol after the five-Breachlord merge failed (Chayula was severed); filled with mindless rage and hunger. PoE1 fought it as Xesht-Ula, the Open Hand; in PoE2 0.5 it is the Breach pinnacle ('Xesht, We That Are One' per a guide), reached through a Breachstone/Realmgate.
sources: Trivia: Xesht is the incomplete fusion of Xoph, Esh, Tul, Uul-Netol; Chayula opposes as the Dreamer
Dialogue "Who is our enemy?": "Xoph... Esh... Tul... Uul-Netol... our melding... failed... They became Xesht."
Lore: failed merge of the five Breachlords; Chayula severed, rest formed Xesht
Lore: failed merge; the rest of the Breachlords formed an incomplete union in the form of Xesht
Xesht: fought by communing with the Dreamer
Xesht, We That Are One: Breach Splinters form a Breachstone, slotted into the Realmgate

alt_summaries.summary: Entity of the Breach (PoE2 wiki: Xesht): the incomplete fusion of four Breachlords (Xoph, Esh, Tul, Uul-Netol) after the planned five-way merger failed; Chayula was severed from the union and opposes it as the Dreamer. Per the Dreamer, Xesht is 'four minds sewn together' filled with endless rage and hunger.

nodes.name: Xoph, Dark Embers
nodes.summary: One of five Breachlords (fire). Boss of Xoph's Domain, accessed via Xoph's Breachstone in a map device (2.5.0; removed from game 3.28.0). Model based on a Marauder; one of four lords fused into Xesht.

nodes.name: Yaomac
nodes.summary: Ancient Vaal god with three serpentine heads, worshipped by Vaalish priests. Ixchel stole his sleeping body for the Order of the Djinn; the Trialmaster refers to Yaomac when the player wins five or more times.

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal shepherd of souls with three serpentine heads who maintains the balance of seasons.
Three-headed serpent Vaal deity, shepherd of Vaal souls and arbiter of the seasons' balance.

nodes.name: Yugul, Reflection of Terror
nodes.summary: Former Vaal scholar of fear who ascended by terrifying children and Vaal leaders; a maw-god killed in the High Gardens.

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal scholar obsessed with fear who used mirrors to petrify terror; ascended through worship; slain by the Exile in Act 8 (Reflection of Terror).
Vaal scholar of fear who ascended to godhood through mirrors that 'petrify fear'; killed by the Exile in PoE1 Act 8.

nodes.name: Ancient Azmeri/Ezomyte Age
aliases: Ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui Era
nodes.summary: Era of the primeval civilisation, Winter of the World, Lightless war and the ancient Azmeri, Ezomyte, Maraketh and Karui peoples, before the Eternal Empire (1 IC).
sources: sections Primeval civilization, The Azmeri, The Maraketh, The Ezomytes
intro paragraph 2; sections 'The Azmeri', 'The Ezomytes', 'The Karui'

alt_summaries.summary: Post-Winter-of-the-World cultures (Azmeri, Maraketh, Ezomyte, Karui) and the Order of the Djinn that defeated the Lightless.

nodes.name: Eternal Empire (era)
nodes.summary: Umbrella period of the Eternal Empire (Sarn Empire) from Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC) through the Reign of Voll to the Cataclysm (~1339 IC). Split into the era_eternal_empire_rise and era_eternal_empire_fall buckets; the faction itself is faction_eternal_empire.
sources: section '===Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)===' (start) and '===The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)===' (end)

nodes.name: Eternal Empire Fall
nodes.summary: The later Eternal Empire: Izaro's Lord's Labyrinth (1317 IC), Chitus and the gemling legions, the Purity Rebellion (1333-1334 IC) and the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) that ends the empire. Boundary with the 'rise' bucket is a convention.
sources: sections 'Reign of Izaro', 'The Purity Rebellion', 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)'

nodes.name: Eternal Empire Rise
nodes.summary: From 1 IC: Tarcus Veruso leads the Azmeri into the lands left by the Vaal and founds Sarn and the Eternal Empire; the empire expands; the Night of a Thousand Ribbons (c. 334 IC) ends Romira's reign.
sources: section 'The Eternal Empire': 'Imperialis Conceptus (1 IC)', 'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Night of a Thousand Ribbons'

nodes.name: Interlude Between Games
nodes.summary: About 20 years between the defeat of Kitava and the PoE2 prelude: Count Geonor, Ogham, and the release of the Seed of Corruption.
sources: section 'Prelude / Count Geonor' ('twenty years after the defeat of Kitava')

nodes.name: PoE2 (era umbrella)
nodes.summary: Umbrella for the PoE2-era buckets: the Acts 1-6 campaign and interludes (era_poe2_campaign) and endgame and league storylines (era_poe2_endgame). Begins after the ~20-year interlude following the PoE1 kill of the Beast. Meta grouping only.

chronology.relative: c. 20 years after the Beast's death

sources: paragraph 3: 'An exile was responsible for killing the Beast around 20 years prior to the events of Path of Exile 2'

nodes.name: PoE2 Campaign
nodes.summary: The PoE2 campaign: the Exile chases the Seed of Corruption across Wraeclast, starting in Ogham (Act 1).

nodes.name: PoE2 Endgame
nodes.summary: PoE2 endgame storylines after the campaign. Not covered in detail in this domain.
sources: section 'Notes' (endgame sections not covered by this domain)

nodes.name: Post-Cataclysm Oriath
nodes.summary: Oriath, the island unaffected by the Cataclysm, becomes a Templar theocracy; the Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius. Roughly 260 years pass before PoE1.

nodes.name: Post-Vaal Dark Age
nodes.summary: Ruins of the Vaal, the surviving Vaal absorbed into the Azmeri, and the Kalguur expedition that colonised and failed on Wraeclast.

chronology.relative: between the Vaal Cataclysm and 1 IC

nodes.name: Precursor Era
nodes.summary: Age of the Precursor civilisation, the only culture wholly predating the Winter of the World; its apex lies further before the Vaal than the Vaal lie before the present.

chronology.relative: before the Winter of the World

alt_summaries.summary: The Precursor civilization, the only culture that wholly predates the Winter of the World, with technology far beyond later peoples.

nodes.name: Primordial Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Earliest prehistory: a molten world with Kalandra trapped in her lake, the Titans, the Winter of the World and the Lightless attack. The wiki says the order of prehistoric events is unclear.

chronology.relative: before the Vaal; earliest prehistory (exact years unknown)

sources: Prehistory: 'When Wraeclast was a primordial molten world of ooze and magma'

alt_summaries.summary: Earliest age of Wraeclast: a molten world of ooze and magma inhabited by Titans, in which Kalandra found her lake. Chronology is explicitly unclear.

nodes.name: Vaal Era
nodes.summary: The Vaal Empire under Queen Atziri, the use of virtue gems and sacrifice, ending in the Vaal Cataclysm.

alt_summaries.summary: Period of the Vaal civilisation up to the Vaal Cataclysm (c. 400 BIC).

nodes.name: Alano Phrecia defeats the dark being
nodes.summary: Alano sealed the dark being in 35 IC; darkness lifted.

nodes.name: Assassination of Chitus
nodes.summary: During the Night of a Thousand Ribbons celebration in Sarn, Victario's rebels ambushed the event. Mayor Ondar, who had gems implanted for it, betrayed Emperor Chitus and killed him.
sources: section 'Assassination of Chitus' (ambush, Ondar betrayal; Origins footnotes)

alt_summaries.summary: Ondar kills Chitus; gemlings fall.

nodes.name: Atziri trapped in the crimson nightmare
nodes.summary: After the Cataclysm Atziri kept her beauty at the cost of her humanity, relegated to a nightmare realm where sacrificed Vaal rise and die repeatedly; her influence later seeps back via Vaal side areas and corruption.

nodes.name: Aul's Final Ritual
nodes.summary: In his last moments Aul rapidly crystallises his citadel with azurite, becoming the Crystal King.
sources: Primeval civilization > Aul: 'In the final moments of his reign, he enacted the final ritual, encasing his palace in crystals'

nodes.name: Aul and Kulemak's Bargain
nodes.summary: Weakened Kulemak offers Aul 'untold power and mastery' for a single golem; the golem is infused with necromancy and the first Lightless/possessed golems result, ultimately toppling the primeval civilisation.

nodes.name: Aul's Uprising
nodes.summary: Aul, a slave, overthrows the tyrant Putembo and becomes the Crystal King.

nodes.name: Release Balbala in Traitor's Passage
nodes.summary: Using Risu's passage, the Exile climbs Traitor's Passage and defeats Balbala, releasing the sealed Djinn.

nodes.name: Battle at the Grain Gate
nodes.summary: Rebel assault led by Victario with Templars, Ezomytes, Maraketh and Karui; repulsed by Chitus' gemlings, Marylene died shielding Victario.

nodes.name: Battle of Lioneye's Watch
nodes.summary: Kaom's ambush kills Lioneye.

nodes.name: Bloody Flowers Rebellion
nodes.summary: 1333 IC Ezomyte victory at Glarryn.

nodes.name: Surrender of Sarn
nodes.summary: Cadiro Perandus negotiates Sarn's unconditional surrender to Voll on 1 Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC after stealing the treasury.

nodes.name: Chitus crowned Emperor
nodes.summary: Crowned 1319 IC; seals Izaro in.

nodes.name: Keth: the Essence of Water
nodes.summary: Following the sand-buried city of Keth, the Exile defeats Azarian, the Forsaken Son, and burns the Water Goddess Halani at her request to recover the Essence of Water.
sources: Walkthrough 'Defeat Azarian' / 'End the Water Goddess' suffering'

nodes.name: Sin creates the Beast
nodes.summary: Sin planted the Dark Ember/Seed of Corruption beneath Highgate and nurtured it into the Beast to suppress the gods and end mortal ascension. PoE2 wiki adds that Sin sought Kalandra's cryptic advice and found the Seed in a Precursor ruin.
sources: paragraph 2: Sin ... sought the ancient being Kalandra ... found a Precursor ruin containing the Seed of Corruption

alt_summaries.summary: Sin plants Dark Ember.

nodes.name: Flame Ruby from the Titan Grotto
nodes.summary: Through the Titan Grotto's Rite of Flame, the Exile defeats Zalmarath, the Colossus, and recovers the Flame Ruby for Zarka.

nodes.name: Daresso leaves Oriath
nodes.summary: c. 1450 IC (History of Wraeclast); contradicts the use of his spirit's Eye of Desire in 1336 IC, which the wiki leaves unexplained.

nodes.name: Death of Geofri
nodes.summary: 1332 IC; Maligaro ambushes templars.

nodes.name: Kaom's march on Highgate and death
nodes.summary: Lured by the Beast's voice posing as Tukohama, Kaom led 500 warriors to Highgate and was deceived into slaying them before dying; his Eye of Fury was taken.
sources: 'Lioneye's Watch' subsection, Kaom's march to Highgate

nodes.name: Defeat of Titucius
nodes.summary: 3rd Galvano of Vitali 1333 IC; Maraketh storm trap.

nodes.name: Deshret seals the mines
nodes.summary: Twenty years after Kaom.

nodes.name: Gemlings fall with Chitus
nodes.summary: With Chitus' death his master gem stopped and the legionnaires linked to his heartbeat died; Captain Alsarus' legion survived beyond the perimeter.

nodes.name: Capture Doryani in the Black Chambers
nodes.summary: The Exile fights through Aggorat to the Black Chambers, rescues Alva, and captures Doryani, who agrees to help contain the Beast with a piece of the Precursor weapon.
sources: Quest 'Capture Doryani for his knowledge of the Beast'

alt_summaries.summary: The Exile defeats Doryani in the Black Chambers; Alva convinces him to follow them to the future and help contain the Beast.

nodes.name: Doryani joins the Exile and the Hooded One in the present
nodes.summary: In the present Doryani confirms he holds one piece of an ancient anti-Corruption weapon; Alva proposes Kingsmarch as a base, and the Hooded One decides the group should travel south to Ngamakanui to find the other pieces.

nodes.name: Board the Dreadnought and defeat Jamanra, the Abomination
nodes.summary: The Exile boards the Dreadnought; Jamanra the Abomination fights, the Countess escapes, and Asala beheads Jamanra. The Beast escapes with the Countess once more.
sources: Quest 'Defeat Jamanra, the Abomination' / 'Speak to Asala'

nodes.name: Earn passage on the Ardura caravan
nodes.summary: The Exile defeats the Sun Clan hyenas and their leader Rathbreaker for Zarka, who admits the Exile to the Ardura akhara as a jingakh.

nodes.name: The Cataclysm
nodes.summary: c. 1339 IC; Malachai takes control of the Beast; Empire falls.
sources: section 'The Cataclysm (~1339 IC)' and 'Reign of Voll'

alt_summaries.summary: Malachai uses the Rapture Device to breach the Belly of the Beast, triggering the Cataclysm around 1339 IC. It ends the Eternal Empire and Voll's reign, and its effects are mostly confined to the Wraeclast landmass.
Eternal Empire's destruction.

nodes.name: Fall of the Primeval Civilization
nodes.summary: The primeval civilisation is toppled by possessed golems (probably the Lightless), as the Winter of the World approaches.

nodes.name: First Kalguuran expedition to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Expedition commissioned by Cadigan III after the Vaal Cataclysm 'Omen'; led by Olroth (Knights of the Sun), Uhtred (Order of the Chalice), Vorana (Black Scythe) and Medved (Druids of the Broken Circle); poisoned journey; colonisation; trade with Karui and Azmeri; gem panic; eventual collapse.

chronology.relative: Thousands of years before PoE1; soon after the Vaal Cataclysm

alt_summaries.summary: Centuries-old expedition ordered by Cadigan III including Knights of the Sun, Black Scythe, Druids of the Broken Circle, Priests of the Chalice and Remembrancers; it taught the Ezomytes runesmithing and ended in tragedy.

nodes.name: Founding of the Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Ahkeli and a dekhara of surviving Maraketh found the Order, using golems and relics of power to push back the Lightless and save the Vastiri Plains.

nodes.name: Founding of Oriath
nodes.summary: Templars banished from the Azmeri found Oriath.

nodes.name: Great Fire
nodes.summary: Ezomyte cataclysm: the First Ones, unhonoured, spill fire out of a mountain; leaders turned to ash, survivors fed on tainted grain from Mother Gull. PoE2 reveals it is the Winter of the World.

nodes.name: Great Wasting
nodes.summary: Karui name for the apocalyptic age of horror and famine also called the Great Fire (Ezomyte) and Winter of the World (Maraketh); Karui ancestors and Maraketh gods are said to emerge in it.

nodes.name: First battle at the Halani Gates
nodes.summary: The Exile opens the gates with Asala; Jamanra, the Risen King, is fought at the gates and retreats behind an impassable sandstorm (Faridun page), while the Countess escapes.
sources: Quest 'Open the third Gate' / 'Return to the Ardura Caravan'

nodes.name: The Hooded One reveals he is Sin
nodes.summary: At a shrine northwest of the caravan, the Hooded One confesses he is Sin, the Thief of Virtue, and that he created the Beast; he sends the Exile south into the long-ago Vaal jungles to find a way to drain the Beast.
sources: Quest log 'Speak to the Hooded One in the Shrine to the Northwest' (quote 'I am... a god. I am the Thief of Virtue. I am Sin.')
[77:11] 'I am the thief of virtue.' / [77:14] 'I am sin.' (Gavryn, Act 2 full dialogue, auto-captions)

nodes.name: Recreate the Horn of the Vastiri
nodes.summary: With Zarka, the Exile reforges the Horn of the Vastiri from the three sub-quest items to counter Jamanra's sandstorm, retracing Orbala's footsteps.
sources: Quest log 'Recreate the Horn of the Vastiri'

nodes.name: Imperialis Conceptus
nodes.summary: Founding of the Eternal Empire (1 IC).

alt_summaries.summary: Tarcus Veruso leads the Azmeri down into the lands left by the Vaal and founds Sarn at 1 IC, marking the start of the Eternal calendar and the Eternal Empire.

nodes.name: Innocence's true ascension (Sanctum relic account)
nodes.summary: Lore revealed through Sanctum unique relics: Sin and Innocence were brothers among the Azmeri; Innocence founded a religion on fear of the 'cleansing fire' and the newcomers' symbol, branded Sin the embodiment of sin, and both ascended (Sin ashen, Innocence golden), until the Azmeri drove Innocence's followers off the mountains. Contradicts the Templar 'mother of two' propaganda.
sources: [24:37]-[32:00] Lycia's relic text account; [43:03]-[44:30] mother of two as fabrication

nodes.name: Kalandra Trapped in the Lake
nodes.summary: Kalandra enters the primordial lake out of curiosity and can never leave: every escape returns her to the lake with no memory.
sources: Lore: Ancient Etchings; History of Wraeclast 'The Lake of Kalandra'

alt_summaries.summary: Kalandra entered the Lake out of curiosity in the primordial era and found herself unable to leave, forgetting each attempt.

nodes.name: Kalguuran Expedition to Wraeclast
nodes.summary: After the Vaal Cataclysm's omens, King Cadigan III sends an expedition with the Triskelion Flame led by Olroth, Uhtred, Vorana and Medved; they colonise Vaal ruins, until horrors, a priesthood plot and the loss of the Flame destroy the colony.

alt_summaries.summary: After the Vaal Cataclysm, a Kalguur expedition (led by Olroth, Uhtred, Vorana and Medved) arrives, colonises, and collapses. The Triskelion Flame is lost and famine follows; the wiki says who sabotaged the port is unknown.

nodes.name: Kaom at Highgate
nodes.summary: Kaom slays his 500 warriors deceived by the Beast.

nodes.name: Kitava invited into Wraeclast
nodes.summary: Karui carvings say the Eternals opened the gate and invited Kitava into the land; Kitava cut the Karui off from the Ancestors. Haku adds that the Karui also had a hand in the downfall.
sources: Weathered Carving in Kaom's Stronghold; Haku 'The Karui and Wraeclast'

nodes.name: Lightless Invasion
nodes.summary: After ash blocked the sun, the Lightless surface and devastate the primeval civilisation, felled Titans and the Maraketh/Azmeri cultures; a coalition under the Third Pact opposes them.
sources: intro; The Winter of the World

nodes.name: Opening of the Lord's Labyrinth
nodes.summary: Izaro opens the maze on 1317 IC; Chitus and Weylin enter; Chitus poisons Weylin.

nodes.name: Lord's Labyrinth Opened
nodes.summary: Izaro opens the Lord's Labyrinth on the second Galvano of Azmeri, 1317 IC. Chitus wins it by betraying Weylin, and then seals Izaro inside.
sources: section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' and 'Reign of Chitus'

nodes.name: Lycia's pact with Beidat
nodes.summary: Lycia, shocked by the unnamed discarded bones of the Templar ossuary and the true origin of Innocence, called Beidat and traded her freedom for immortality inside the Sanctum, giving the Scourge a foothold in Wraeclast.

nodes.name: Slay Count Geonor in Ogham Manor
nodes.summary: The Exile infiltrates Ogham Manor and kills Count Geonor, freeing Ogham; Oriana escapes with the Beast, and the Hooded One sends the Exile east toward the Vastiri.
sources: Quest 'Kill the Mad Wolf' / 'Return to Town'

nodes.name: Malachai spared by Voll
nodes.summary: Malachai promises end of thaumaturgy.

nodes.name: Maraketh Golden Age
nodes.summary: Roughly a thousand years of glory after Solerai and Lundara expelled the Lightless, in a lush Vastiri of seven rivers; ended when the Beast silenced the gods.

nodes.name: Drain the lake through the Matlan Waterways
nodes.summary: The Exile powers the Infested Barrens altar with the large Soul Core and activates the Matlan Waterways, revealing the Sunken City of Utzaal.
sources: Quest 'Activate The Matlan Waterways' / 'Talk to Alva'

nodes.name: Rudja and the Faridun defector at Mawdun Mine
nodes.summary: At Mawdun Quarry and Mine, the Exile defeats Rudja and frees the defector Risu, who reveals Jamanra's plan to feed the Beast and that the Halani Gates are closed.
sources: Quest 'Defeat Rudja, Dread Engineer' / 'Talk to Risu about the closed Gates'

nodes.name: Medved's challenge
nodes.summary: A two-axe horror leader (recognised by Vorana as her beloved Medved) killed 42 challengers in 42 days; Vorana ordered a retreat; two villages fell.

nodes.name: Night of a Thousand Ribbons
nodes.summary: Burning of Sarn in protest against Romira; later festival where Chitus was assassinated.

alt_summaries.summary: Around 334 IC, Sarn burns in protest at Emperor Romira's cannibal banquet and incest, and Romira is deposed. The date is still celebrated after reconstruction.

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn Forsake Kalandra
nodes.summary: The Order of the Djinn swears to free Kalandra and devotes itself to her artefacts of power, but 'once they understood the truth of this place' its scribes try to erase her from history, burning their books (Kalandra page: and self-immolating out of fear); the History page words it as forsaking and abandoning her.
sources: Lore > Ancient Etchings: 'burning their books and self-immolating out of fear'

nodes.name: Oriath destroyed by Sirus
nodes.summary: PoE1 Conquerors of the Atlas: Oriath is completely destroyed by Sirus, leaving it devastated; PoE2 states the world believed Oriath abandoned twenty years ago after crises.

alt_summaries.summary: Sirus used his own map device to enter Oriath and burn it down; Kirac took a blow meant for Zana; the Exile defeated him. In Siege timeline an unknown exile dealt Sirus a near-fatal blow at the cost of her life.

nodes.name: Original Sin (Innocence's ascension)
nodes.summary: Per Lycia's relics, twin brothers Innocence and Sin lived among the Azmeri; Innocence, unable to attract enough followers, turned his followers against Sin and used their hatred to ascend, leaving Sin blackened. The Templar stained-glass version is propaganda.
sources: section on Forbidden Sanctum relics / Lycia's findings; 'Original Sin' unique
[24:43]-[25:12] Lycia's story of Sin and Innocence among the Azmeri

alt_summaries.summary: Innocence turns followers against Sin.

nodes.name: Perpetual Night over the Imperial Heartlands
nodes.summary: Azmerian writers describe part of the empire cast into perpetual night, a 'dark being' dismembering Emperor Caspiro, until General Alano Phrecia dispelled it, 'returning the gaze of Solaris'. Likely the darkness later sealed in the Oversoul (per GGG Q&A).

chronology.relative: Caspiro died ~5 years after Veruso; Alano Phrecia quote dated first Sacrato of Lurici, 35 IC

sources: Alano Phrecia quote: '... our legions drove the dark being deep into the recesses of its lair and sealed it away for eternity' (35 IC)

nodes.name: Plague of Ezomyr
nodes.summary: At some point most of Ezomyr was wiped out by a plague (per Kahuturoa), after Oriath was recently established.

nodes.name: The Trials of Chaos (PoE2 Act 3 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 3 quest: after obtaining an Inscribed Ultimatum (or the Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian), the Exile places it in the Temple of Chaos offering and completes the Trialmaster's Challenges for 2 Ascendancy Points. The PoE2 entry point to the Trial of Chaos ascension trial.
sources: Infobox (act 3, optional, start 'Acquire an Inscribed Ultimatum', boss Xyclucian, the Chimera); '===Place the Inscribed Ultimatum in the Temple Offering===' and '===Quest Complete=== (2 Ascendancy Points)'
Access section (Chimeral Inscribed Ultimatum from Xyclucian; Temple of Chaos offering); lead ('based on Ultimatum from PoE1')

nodes.name: Exile travels to Utzaal's past
nodes.summary: The Exile and Alva use the gateway to reach Utzaal before the Cataclysm to learn of the Beast.

nodes.name: Arrival in Kingsmarch
nodes.summary: Exile, Hooded One and Doryani reach Kingsmarch to find the Weapon; Doryani laments science never recovered; the Hooded One says the Kalguurans 'have potential'.

nodes.name: Alliance plan against Oriath
nodes.summary: The Hooded One decides to call the Ezomytes, Maraketh and Vaal (Doryani's reserves) to war before assaulting Oriath; the Karui are already allied.

nodes.name: Exile defeats Benedictus
nodes.summary: In the Excavation the Countess leaves Benedictus to hold the Exile; he is defeated, and Kanu, begging to be taken along, reveals the Beast is in Oriath before Tavakai strikes him down.
sources: Confront Kanu and the First Herald; Defeat Benedictus

alt_summaries.summary: Act 4: after the Countess flees to Oriath, the Exile defeats Benedictus in the Excavation; Kanu then names Oriath and is killed by Tavakai.

nodes.name: Tavakai defeated at Heart of the Tribe
nodes.summary: Tavakai fights in three phases; Tukohama rejects him ('This... is not the Way'); the Exile defeats him.

nodes.name: Exile defeats Torvian
nodes.summary: On Arastas the Exile defeats Torvian, Hand of the Saviour, after the Twilight Order ambush at the church.
sources: Defeat Torvian, Hand of the Saviour

alt_summaries.summary: Act 4: the Exile defeats Torvian, Hand of the Saviour on Arastas.

nodes.name: Freeing the Trickster at Journey's End
nodes.summary: Exile frees 'Freya Hartlin' with Verisium Spikes; she reveals herself as Tangmazu, triggering a Delirium encounter with Omniphobia.

nodes.name: Charter of the Aurora May
nodes.summary: Alva introduces Rog, who sells a Boat Charter for Vaal treasure; Makoru and Kanu will take the Exile to the most dangerous islands.
sources: Talk to Alva; Take the Boat Charter

nodes.name: Island search for weapon pieces
nodes.summary: The Exile sails the Karui islands (e.g. Isle of Kin, Shrike Island, Whakapanu, Abandoned Prison) to find the three Weapon pieces, whose island locations rotate; bosses include Krutog, Diamora, the Prisoner and the Scourge of the Skies. Kedge Bay is separate Dark Mists content.

nodes.name: Hooded One recalls Precursor script
nodes.summary: On the first and second Weapon pieces the Hooded One recognises Precursor writing from a faded mortal memory (a woman's lap, a vivid book; later: sent to live among the Azmeri with a brother and sister, but earlier 'somewhere else' with works of stone, metal and glass).
sources: Witness the Hooded One (1st and 2nd pieces)
Witness The Hooded One (first and second pieces)

alt_summaries.summary: Weapon pieces carry Precursor writing the Hooded One partly recognises from a mortal childhood: a book in a woman's lap, life 'somewhere else' with stone, metal and glass before being sent to the Azmeri with his brother and sister.

nodes.name: Weapon reforged; Third Edict revealed
aliases: The Weapon is reforged; Third Edict revealed
nodes.summary: In the Excavated Site the Hooded One reforges the Weapon and Tavakai seizes it; back in Kingsmarch the Hooded One reads the inscription 'The instrument of the Third Edict', made to cleanse Corruption and destroy the Beast.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon; Return to Kingsmarch

alt_summaries.summary: The Hooded One reforges the Weapon in the Excavated Site; Tavakai seizes it. Back in Kingsmarch the Hooded One reads the inscription: 'The instrument of the Third Edict.'

nodes.name: Sin cures Tavakai and Makoru
nodes.summary: The Hooded One, called Sin in the quest log, cures Tavakai and Makoru of Blood Fever with the Weapon; Tavakai pledges the Karui to fight Oriana.
sources: Witness Sin cure Tavakai and Makoru

nodes.name: Tavakai seizes the Weapon
nodes.summary: After the reforging Tavakai takes the Weapon for the Karui and flees to Ngakanu with Makoru; the Hooded One warns of its Corruption.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon

nodes.name: Utopia on Arastas
nodes.summary: Missionary Lorandis sends the Exile to Arastas to swear an oath to the Saviour; Servitor Marius offers Utopia; refusal completes the quest, and Benedictus and Kanu's treachery follow.

nodes.name: Infiltrating Oriath (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Datamined Act 5 Normal quest listed by PoE2DB after The Siege of Oriath; the table gives no description. Unconfirmed until Act 5 is released.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'Infiltrating Oriath' row (Normal; reward none listed)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: No Rest for the Blighted (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Datamined Act 5 Normal quest listed by PoE2DB; its reward is labelled [DNT-UNUSED] Blighted Core Bomb, so it may not be in the live game.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'No Rest for the Blighted' row (Normal; reward [DNT-UNUSED] Blighted Core Bomb)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: Assault on Oriath (planned Act 5)
nodes.summary: Announced Act 5: arrive in Oriath hunting the Beast; datamined quests The Siege of Oriath, Infiltrating Oriath, etc.

nodes.name: Pinned Down (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Datamined Act 5 Normal quest listed by PoE2DB; reward Reefsteel Greaves. No description in the datamine.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'Pinned Down' row (Normal; reward Reefsteel Greaves)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: Pleasure and Pain (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Datamined Act 5 Normal quest listed by PoE2DB; reward Rogue's Marker x5. No description in the datamine.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'Pleasure and Pain' row (Normal; reward Rogue's Marker x5)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: Plumbing the Depths (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Optional datamined Act 5 quest: Elwynian reports a water-supply problem and asks the Exile to make their way to the Cisterns to investigate; reward Scroll of Wisdom.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'Plumbing the Depths' row (Optional; reward Scroll of Wisdom)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: Trarthan Gladiator (PoE2 Act 5, datamined)
nodes.summary: Optional datamined Act 5 quest: travel to the Plaza of Patrons; reward Detailed Mitts.
sources: Act 5 Quest table: 'Trarthan Gladiator' row (Optional; reward Detailed Mitts)
Act 5 section: '(planned for full release)' (wiki lists no Act 5 quests)

nodes.name: Death in the Ranges (Forbidden Rites)
nodes.summary: Released Forbidden Rites Ritual set for Interlude 3 (Kriar Village, Glacial Tarn, Howling Caves): unique-boss Rituals in each area; completing the set offers a choice of unique items. Not an Act 6 story quest.
sources: Ritual sets list: 'Death in the Ranges'

nodes.name: Sands of Ruin (Forbidden Rites)
nodes.summary: Released Forbidden Rites Ritual set for Interlude 2 (The Khari Crossing, Sel Khari Sanctuary, The Galai Gates): unique-boss Rituals in each area; completing the set offers a choice of unique items. Not an Act 6 story quest.

nodes.name: Shadow Over Ogham (Forbidden Rites)
nodes.summary: Released Forbidden Rites Ritual set for Interlude 1 (Scorched Farmlands, Holten, Wolvenhold): unique-boss Rituals in each area; completing the set offers a choice of unique items. Not an Act 6 story quest.

nodes.name: Abandoned Prison (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Required Act 4 side quest, begun by speaking to Makoru: the Exile goes through the Eternal Empire's Abandoned Prison to Solitary Confinement and kills The Prisoner, who holds one of the three Precursor weapon pieces needed for The Search.
sources: Infobox (required: Yes, act 4, completion 'Kill The Prisoner'); lead ('the Prisoner holds one of the three weapon pieces'); quest log '===Slay the Prisoner===' and '===Quest Complete==='

nodes.name: Ancient Beacons (quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Fate of the Vaal league quest (0.4.0) that introduces Atziri's Temple. The Exile finds Ancient Beacons surrounded by monsters, sacrifices those monsters and activates beacons (the first, then five, four, three, two and one more), enters the Vaal Ruins, and uses the Temple Console to build and open the first Temple.

chronology.relative: PoE2 endgame (Fate of the Vaal league, 0.4.0)

sources: infobox (start 'Find an Ancient Beacon', completion 'Open a Temple'); Walkthrough 'Sacrifice the Monsters' and 'Activate five additional Beacons' ... 'Use the Temple Console'; Quest Complete 'You have cleansed Ancient Beacons, built and opened your first Temple'

nodes.name: Ancient Gateway and the Fortress Gateways
nodes.summary: After the Fortress rises, the Exile travels to the Ancient Gateway, uses levers to reach the central platform, summons Doryani and activates another Precursor Beacon, which opens the way to the Burning Monolith (quest log, Legacy of the Precursors).
sources: quest log: 'Travel to the Ancient Gateway', 'Defeat the Precursor Separator', 'Ride the Elevator'

nodes.name: Gods awaken after the Beast's death
nodes.summary: About 20 years before PoE2 an exile killed the Beast, waking the slumbering gods, who per the Twilight Order now make civilisation impossible.

nodes.name: Waking the Dreamer
nodes.summary: 0.5 Breach story: travel to the Monastery of the Keepers and the Genesis Tree; defeat It That Was Tul and It That Was Esh (Sky Fortress bosses; official notes: they yield the key to the Breach pinnacle) and retrieve the Breachlord Sac to reach the Dreamer; later fight Xesht. Hiveborn details come from press coverage.
sources: After defeating It That Was Esh and It That Was Tul and retrieving the Breachlord Sac
Tul and Esh are fortress bosses; defeating them yields a key to the Breach Pinnacle boss

nodes.name: The Burning Monolith
nodes.summary: Endgame site reached during Legacy of the Precursors ('Reach the Burning Monolith') after the Ancient Gateway. In 0.1-0.4 it was found directly on the Atlas and opened with three Crisis Fragments (The Pinnacle of Flame); in 0.5 it stands inside the Precursor Fortress.
sources: 'Reach the Burning Monolith', 'Return to the Burning Monolith'
Find The Burning Monolith on the endgame map; obtain three Crisis Fragments to open the locked door

nodes.name: Clearing the Way (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Interlude 2 quest: Risu asks the Exile to slay the scorpion Akthi, the Final Sting, and the sandworm Anundr at the far end of the Khari Crossing so the other akharas can join the Gifting of Water. The reward is a Book of Specialisation.
sources: Infobox (optional, act 'interlude', start 'Speak to Risu at the Khari Bazaar', objective 'Defeat Akthi, the Final Sting and Anundr, the Sandworm'); quest log '===Defeat Akthi and Anundr===' and '===Quest Complete==='; Quest.wiki Interludes list

nodes.name: Cracks in the Earth (PoE2 quest, removed)
nodes.summary: Former optional Act 1 quest from Mortimer in Clearfell Encampment, exclusive to the Rise of the Abyssal league: the Exile seeks the source of abyssal monsters, which leads to the Mud Burrow and an Abyss. The quest has been removed from the game.
sources: Quest infobox ('historical content', act 1, 'Speak to Mortimer'); '===Find the source of Abyssal Monsters===' and '===Quest Complete===' (intro: 'It was exclusive to Rise of the Abyssal league'; Version history 0.3.0 'Introduced to the game', 0.4.0 'Removed from the game')

nodes.name: Dark Mists (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Act 4 quest from Tujen: clear the fog at Kedge Bay (Captain Hartlin), bring Verisium to Dannig and return to Tujen.

nodes.name: Defeating the Arbiter of Ash
aliases: Arbiter of Ash defeated; Flame Seed stolen
nodes.summary: The Exile kills the Arbiter of Ash at the Burning Monolith. In 0.5 it is a quest boss inside the Fortress and no longer the apex; afterwards a mysterious rider on a wyrm (Tecrod) steals the Flame Seed.
sources: Lore: Mysterious Entity riding a wyrm steals the Flame Seed after the Arbiter of Ash is defeated

alt_summaries.summary: Precursor guardian of the Flame Seed falls in the Burning Monolith arena; a wyrm-riding figure (Tecrod) takes the Flame Seed, saying 'This power serves a new master...'.

nodes.name: Arbiter of Divinity destroys Tecrod; First Edict averted
nodes.summary: In the Origin Tower the Exile places the Origin Core; Tecrod's wyrm incapacitates the Exile and Tecrod exults 'With this, the Master shall know unending power!'; the Arbiter of Divinity destroys Tecrod's body ('Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!') and is then fought by the Exile (quest step 141).
sources: his body is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity

alt_summaries.summary: At the top of the Origin Tower the Exile fights the Arbiter of Divinity (quest step 141); quest complete: 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.'

nodes.name: Western and Eastern Gateways, Enigma Chambers: Count Geonor and Doryani
nodes.summary: From the Burning Monolith the Exile clears the Western Gateway (guardian: Precursor Separator) and Eastern Gateway (Precursor Refiner) via levers, then fights Count Geonor in the Western Enigma Chamber (Ancient Crisis Fragment) and Doryani in the Eastern Enigma Chamber (Weathered Crisis Fragment) (quest log; this section of the wiki log is in a hidden comment block, so medium confidence). The Doryani and Geonor fights echo the Citadel bosses of 0.1-0.4.
sources: 'Defeat Count Geonor', 'Defeat Doryani', 'Pick up the Ancient Crisis Fragment', 'Pick up the Weathered Crisis Fragment'
Enigma Chambers drop the two Crisis Fragments

nodes.name: Doryani's Waygate
nodes.summary: Doryani introduces and activates a Waygate on Precursor leylines at the Ziggurat; Waystones and the Map Device open the endgame Atlas. Who originally built the Waygate is not stated.

nodes.name: Exile Escapes Ogham
aliases: Exile sentenced to hang in Ogham
nodes.summary: Count Geonor sentences the PoE2 Exile to death. The Exile narrowly escapes the Executioner's hanging by jumping into the ocean.

alt_summaries.summary: Count Geonor sentences the Exile to death; the Executioner tries to hang them, and the Exile escapes by jumping into the ocean.

nodes.name: Ezomyte Infiltration (PoE2 quest, removed)
nodes.summary: Former Epilogue quest started by investigating The Burning Monolith; the boss is The Perennial King. The wiki marks it as historical content, removed from the game.
sources: Infobox (act 'Epilogue', start 'Investigate The Burning Monolith', boss The Perennial King); '{{Historical content}}' and 'Removed from the game'

nodes.name: Faridun Foray (PoE2 quest, removed)
nodes.summary: Former Epilogue quest started by investigating The Burning Monolith; the boss is Count Geonor. The wiki marks it as historical content, removed from the game.
sources: Infobox (act 'Epilogue', start 'Investigate The Burning Monolith', boss Count Geonor); '{{Historical content}}' and 'Removed from the game'

nodes.name: Fate of the Vaal questline
nodes.summary: League quest in which Alva and Doryani open Atziri's Temple as a time portal; the Exile defeats Xipocado, the Red Queen and Fell Serpent but fails to stop the Cataclysm.

nodes.name: Fate of the Vaal (quest)
nodes.summary: Quest (0.4 league): with Doryani and Alva the Exile uses the Temple Console to open Atziri's Temple (Doryani turns the entrance into a time portal), defeats Xipocado and the Royal Architect, then Atziri the Red Queen and Atziri the Fell Serpent in The Cradle, and takes Atziri's Medallion; the wiki's completion text: you failed to stop the Vaal Cataclysm.

chronology.relative: Quest obtained in Act 4 after unlocking Atziri's Temple and recruiting Doryani (0.4 league)

sources: Quest Complete: 'You have defeated Atziri, the Red Queen... but you failed to stop the Vaal Cataclysm.'

nodes.name: Finding the Forge (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 1 quest in Ogham Village: the Exile finds Renly's Smithing Tools and returns them, which restores his Salvage Bench and gives a choice of a lesser rune. Can be completed once per league.
sources: Quest infobox ('act 1', start 'Talk to Renly', objective 'Find Smithing Tools in Ogham Village'); '===Quest Complete===' (Salvage Bench restored)

nodes.name: Geonor seizes the Seed from the Hooded One
nodes.summary: Opening cinematic: Count Geonor impales the Hooded One with a runic sword, takes the sphere holding the Seed of Corruption and shouts 'Bind him!'; Countess later reveals she was behind him.

nodes.name: Hilda's Hunting (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Required epilogue endgame quest tied to Hilda: automatically started near Hilda's Campsite, the Exile finds Hilda and defeats four Great Beasts in turn, speaking with her between fights; the quest completes after the fourth. The wiki page is a stub; quest steps are listed without rewards.
sources: Infobox (required: Yes, act 'epilogue', start 'Reach Hilda's Campsite'); quest log '===Defeat the first Great Beast===' and '===Speak to Hilda===' entries (stub page)

nodes.name: Hostile Takeover (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Ange's Act 4 quest to clear the Shoreline Hideout.

nodes.name: Recruit the Ezomytes (Curse of Holten)
nodes.summary: Exile kills Isolde, Heldra, Siora, then Thane Wulfric and Lady Elswyth, ending Holten's blight; Renly pledges all clans to the war.

nodes.name: Recruit the Maraketh (The Stolen Barya)
nodes.summary: Exile defeats Elzarah, Vornas and Prince Azmadi to save the First Barya; Asala completes the Gifting of Water and brings the Maraketh to Kingsmarch.

nodes.name: Recruit the Vaal (Doryani's Contingency)
nodes.summary: The code phrase 'the time of the sparrow has come' and defeat of Rakkar, Stormgore, Zolin and Zelina secures the Cuachic.

alt_summaries.summary: In the Interlude the Exile reaches Mount Kriar, defeats Zolin and Zelina and secures Cuachic aid.

nodes.name: Landing at the Ziggurat Refuge
nodes.summary: Siege of Oriath ends not at Oriath but at the Ziggurat Refuge; Quest Complete text says 'despite your attempts to travel to Oriath'. Why is not stated; the Beast's corruption holds the Hooded One in thrall afterwards.
sources: Doryani: Beast's Corruption holds the Hooded One

nodes.name: Vessel of Kulemak
nodes.summary: Pinnacle Abyss encounter, the Vessel of Kulemak: Kulemak's Invitation (dropped by Abyssal commanders per guides) sends the player into the Well and the Black Cathedral. Guides say defeating it unlocks the Abyssal Lich ascendancy (exact conditions vary by guide/patch); fully empowering it means defeating the Lich Lords Kurgal, Ulaman and Amanamu.
sources: Vessel of Kulemak: Tasgul and Vandroth drop Kulemak Invitation; empower via Kurgal, Ulaman, Amanamu

nodes.name: Land of the Kin (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Required Act 4 side quest, begun by speaking to Makoru and sailing to the Isle of Kin; the Exile explores the Isle and Volcanic Warrens to kill Krutog, Lord of Kin. Part of the rotating Act 4 requirements.
sources: Infobox (required: Yes, act 4, start 'Sailing to Isle of Kin', completion 'Kill Krutog, Lord of Kin'); lead; quest log '===Explore the Isle of Kin===' to '===Quest Complete==='

nodes.name: Legacy of the Maji (endgame quest)
nodes.summary: Endgame quest begun by finding Aoife near a Ritual Altar: she was killed by the King in the Mists (the King of the Nameless); the Exile destroys his effigies, kills him again at the Crux of Nothingness, takes his Head and Aoife's body, performs the Rite of the Nameless over five maps and defeats the Bodach. Quest complete: 'You have defeated The Bodach and Aoife is finally at peace.' (steps from a hidden comment block).

nodes.name: Legacy of the Precursors (endgame quest)
nodes.summary: The primary PoE2 endgame quest: the Hooded One sleeps, held in thrall by the Beast's Corruption; Doryani proposes recovering Precursor knowledge via the Waygate, leading to the Precursor Tower, the Fortress, the Burning Monolith, the Arbiter of Ash and (0.5) the Arbiter of Divinity.

chronology.relative: Immediately after the PoE2 campaign (post-Siege of Oriath)

sources: lead: primary endgame quest obtained immediately upon reaching the endgame; quest log 'Check on the Hooded One' / 'Speak to Doryani'

alt_summaries.summary: First endgame quest (0.5.0): the Hooded One lies in Corruption-induced sleep and Doryani, with the Waygate, begins the search for ancient knowledge.

0.5.0 endgame quest: the Hooded One lies in corruption-induced sleep; Doryani leads the hunt through Enigma Chambers, Arbiter of Ash, Fourth Edict, Origin Tower, and the Arbiter of Divinity, ending 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.'

nodes.name: Ngamahu's Test (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 4 Test of Mettle in the Halls of the Dead, started at the Hinekora Totem: three waves of enemies, then a Blank Tattoo of Ngamahu is turned in for a permanent choice of +5 Strength or +5% Fire Resistance (cannot be changed).
sources: Infobox (act 4, optional, start 'Enter Ngamahu's Test in Halls of the Dead'); lead ('one of the three additional Tests of Mettle'); Rewards: 'Strength Tattoo of Ngamahu (+5 Strength) or Fire Tattoo of Ngamahu (+5% Fire Resistance)'

nodes.name: The Origin Core and the Origin Tower
nodes.summary: Combining the Origin Cradle and Origin Spark (from the Matriarch and Patriarch Halls) in the Precursor Reactor yields the Origin Core; when the Exile places it in the Origin Tower, Tecrod's wyrm incapacitates the Exile and Tecrod exults 'With this, the Master shall know unending power!' before the Arbiter of Divinity destroys his body.
sources: Lore: when the player places the Origin Core into the Origin Tower, Tecrod's wyrm incapacitates the character
Matriarch and Patriarch Halls drop Origin Cradle and Origin Spark; combine into Origin Core at the Precursor Reactor

nodes.name: The Pinnacle of Flame (removed quest)
nodes.summary: Epilogue/endgame quest of 0.1-0.4: find the Burning Monolith on the endgame map and collect three Crisis Fragments to open the door to the Arbiter of Ash. Removed in 0.5.0 and folded into Legacy of the Precursors.
sources: Walkthrough and Version history: 0.1.0 introduced, 0.5.0 removed

nodes.name: The Patriarch and Matriarch Halls
nodes.summary: After the Arbiter of Ash falls and the Origin Tower is explored, Doryani sends the Exile to the Patriarch and Matriarch Halls: defeat Phyx, Sentinel of the Spark (Origin Spark) and Phya, Sentinel of the Cradle (Origin Cradle); the two are combined in the Precursor Reactor into the Origin Core. Source steps sit in a hidden comment block of the quest log (medium).
sources: steps 112-137: 'Defeat Phyx, Sentinel of the Spark', 'Defeat Phya, Sentinel of the Cradle', 'Pick up the Origin Spark/Cradle', 'Activate the Precursor Reactor', 'Pick up the Origin Core'

nodes.name: Activating the Precursor Tower
nodes.summary: The Exile reaches a Precursor Tower and activates its beacon; an Irradiated Tablet drops and (in 0.5) the Precursor Fortress rises from the ground in a cinematic.
sources: Activate the Precursor Beacon: 'An Irradiated Tablet will drop, and the Precursor Fortress will rise from the ground in a cinematic.'

nodes.name: PoE2 1.0 full release
nodes.summary: Announced at Gamescom Opening Night Live (Aug 2026): Path of Exile 2 leaves Early Access on 2026-12-11 with a six-act campaign (Acts 5 and 6 new). Meta/release fact, not an in-world event.

nodes.name: The Runeseeker (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Act 4 quest from Farrow: collect Torn Map Pieces for Dannig, unlocking Plunder's Point and Runeforging.

nodes.name: Shrike Island (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Required Act 4 side quest, begun by speaking to Makoru and sailing to Shrike Island; the Exile explores the island and kills the unique Scourge of the Skies. Part of the rotating Act 4 requirements.
sources: Infobox (required: Yes, act 4, start 'Sailing to Shrike Island', completion 'Kill the Scourge of the Skies'); lead ('secondary main story quest'); '===Kill the Scourge of the Skies==='

nodes.name: Siege of Oriath
nodes.summary: Act 4 quest unlocked after the three Interludes: the Hooded One says Wraeclast has united and proposes an assault on Oriath, but the Exile ends up at the Ziggurat Refuge, where the endgame begins.
sources: infobox: completion 'End up at the Ziggurat Refuge'
Quest Complete: 'If we do manage to stop the Twilight Order and slay the Beast...'

alt_summaries.summary: After all three Interludes the Hooded One plans the assault on Oriath; sailing there ends instead at the Ziggurat Refuge. The wiki infobox files the quest under Act 4.
Act 4 quest unlocked after the three Interludes: the Karui, Ezomytes, Maraketh and Vaal are united against the Twilight Order, but the attempt to sail to Oriath ends instead at the Ziggurat Refuge.

nodes.name: Strange Reflection (endgame quest)
nodes.summary: Delirium endgame quest started by freeing Elder Madox from a Delirium mirror; leads to the Withered Willow, and ends with defeating the Raven Trickster (Tangmazu).
sources: infobox: start Find Elder Madox in a map; completion Defeat The Raven Trickster

nodes.name: Tasalio's Test (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 4 Test of Mettle in the Halls of the Dead, started at the Hinekora Totem: three waves of enemies, then a Blank Tattoo of Tasalio is turned in for a permanent choice of +5 Intelligence or +5% Cold Resistance (cannot be changed).
sources: Infobox (act 4, optional, start 'Enter Tasalio's Test in Halls of the Dead'); lead ('one of the three additional Tests of Mettle'); Rewards: 'Intelligence Tattoo of Tasalio (+5 Intelligence) or Cold Tattoo of Tasalio (+5% Cold Resistance)'

nodes.name: Tawhoa's Test (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 4 Test of Mettle in the Halls of the Dead, started at the Hinekora Totem: three waves of enemies, then a Blank Tattoo of Tawhoa is turned in for a permanent choice of +5 Dexterity or +5% Lightning Resistance (cannot be changed).
sources: Infobox (act 4, optional, start 'Enter Tawhoa's Test in Halls of the Dead'); lead ('one of the three additional Tests of Mettle'); Rewards: 'Dexterity Tattoo of Tawhoa (+5 Dexterity) or Lightning Tattoo of Tawhoa (+5% Lightning Resistance)'

nodes.name: The Grand Expedition (quest)
nodes.summary: Endgame quest (start: Speak to Farrow): Farrow fears for Kingsmarch; the Exile uses Makoru's logbook to find Gwennen, defeats Medved, the Fallen Seer, Vorana, Last to Fall and Uhtred, the Stardrinker, then searches for Olroth via logbooks passed through Dannig, Tujen and Rog (steps in a hidden comment block). Wiki infobox completion: 'Defeat The Aberration'.

alt_summaries.summary: Endgame quest in which Farrow worries about Kingsmarch after the chaos and the Exile returns to the Ruins of Kingsmarch to find Dannig, Gwennen, Tujen and Rog and the logbooks of Vorana, Uhtred and Olroth, recovering the Shattered Triskelion.

nodes.name: The Hunt Begins (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 1 quest in the Hunting Grounds: Delwyn, an Azmeri hunter, has the Exile track a Spirit wisp to a hunted monster, which introduces the Azmeri Spirit encounter.
sources: Quest infobox ('act 1', optional); '===Speak to Delwyn===' and '===Quest Complete===' (Version history 0.3.0: 'Azmeri Spirits now start appearing from Hunting Grounds')

nodes.name: The Lost Lute (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 1 quest begun by Una after The Mysterious Shade: the Exile searches Una's family hut in Ogham Farmlands for her carved lute and returns it to her at Clearfell Encampment for a Book of Specialisation and two Weapon Set passive skill points.
sources: Quest infobox; '===Search for Una's Lute===' and '===Return the Lute to Una===' quest log; '===Quest Complete===' (Book of Specialisation, two Weapon Set Passive Skill Points)

nodes.name: The Search (PoE2 Act 4)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Act 4 main quest: the Exile, Doryani, Alva and the Hooded One reach Kingsmarch, hire a boat (Makoru of the Aurora May, under the Meridian Free Traders) and seek the three pieces of the Precursor weapon, ending with Tavakai.

nodes.name: The Slithering Dead (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 3 quest: Servi asks the Exile to find the source of the Azakh-Kul poison; in the Venom Crypts' Den of the Serpent Priestess the Exile finds Corpse-snake Venom, which Servi turns into a Venom Draught, giving a permanent choice of Stun Threshold, Elemental Ailment Threshold or Mana Regeneration.
sources: Infobox (act 3, start 'Entering the Venom Crypts'); quest logs '===Take the Corpse-snake Venom===' and '===Take a Venom Draught===' ; Rewards section

nodes.name: The Trail of Corruption (Act 2 quest)
nodes.summary: Act 2 main quest: the Hooded One and Sekhema Asala pursue the Beast's trail of Corruption across the Vastiri desert from the Ardura Caravan, through Mawdun Mine, Traitor's Passage and the Halani Gates, the Horn of the Vastiri and Deshar, to the Dreadnought where Jamanra, the Abomination is defeated. Distinct from the Act 1 quest event_trail_of_corruption_act1.
sources: Infobox (act 2, start 'Enter the Ardura Caravan'); Rewards section; quest log headings '===Speak to the Hooded One===' through '===Quest Complete===' (pursuit of Jamanra, the Abomination)
Act 2 list: 'The Trail of Corruption (Act 2)' with sub-quests 'A Theft of Ivory', 'The City of Seven Waters' and 'A Crown of Stone' nested under it

nodes.name: Treacherous Ground (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 1 quest: Renly asks the Exile to find and kill the Devourer in its Mud Burrow beneath Clearfell so the Ezomytes can leave the walls; the reward is a level 1 Uncut Support Gem and 100 gold.
sources: Quest infobox ('required: No', act 1, start 'Talk to Renly'); '===Slay the Devourer===' walkthrough; '===Talk to Renly for your reward===' and '===Quest Complete==='

nodes.name: Treasures of Utzaal (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 3 quest begun by Oswald: monkey statues lead to The Molten Vault, where the Exile defeats Mektul, the Forgemaster, who drops The Hammer of Kamasa; returning the hammer to Oswald unlocks the Reforging Bench.
sources: Infobox (act 3, start 'Summon Oswald in front of the Molten Vault', completion 'Bring The Hammer of Kamasa to Oswald'); '===Speak to Oswald===' quote on the Monkey God (Kamasa); '===Defeat Mektul, the Forgemaster===' and '===Quest Complete==='

nodes.name: Trial of the Ancestors (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional PoE2 Act 4 quest unlocked by freeing Matiki; the Exile meets Hinekora in the Trial of the Ancestors and receives the Tattoo of Hinekora.

alt_summaries.summary: Matiki's rescue leads to Tests of Mettle, Yama's trial and Hinekora, who offers 'Her power... if you will accept it.'

nodes.name: Tribal Medicine (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 4 quest from Kaimana in Ngakanu: the Exile fetches a Shark Fin from the Great White One on Whakapanu Island so Kaimana can make an elixir against the Blood Fever. The reward is a permanent choice of Kaom's Lesson or Rakiata's Lesson.
sources: Infobox (act 4, optional, start 'Picking up Shark Fin', completion 'Deliver the Shark Fin to Kaimana'); lead; Rewards (Kaom's Lesson / Rakiata's Lesson, 'cannot be changed'); quest logs '===Speak to Kaimana==='

nodes.name: Tribal Vengeance (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Optional Act 3 quest in The Azak Bog: Servi asks the Exile to slay Ignagduk, the Bog Witch, at Gor-gor Mog to free the stolen children of her tribe, then to return her Ghastly Spear to Servi for a magic charm.
sources: Infobox (act 3, boss Ignagduk, the Bog Witch); quest logs '===Talk to Servi===' and '===Kill Ignagduk==='; Rewards section (charms)

nodes.name: Vaal Incursion (PoE2 quest, removed)
nodes.summary: Former Epilogue quest started by investigating The Burning Monolith; the boss is Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge. The wiki marks it as historical content, removed from the game.
sources: Infobox (act 'Epilogue', start 'Investigate The Burning Monolith', boss Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge); '{{Historical content}}' and 'Removed from the game'

nodes.name: Testing the Waygate
nodes.summary: Doryani has the Exile run the first Waystone map; he had not tested the Waygate beforehand ('Science is a process').
sources: quest steps 'Select and enter a Map' / Doryani 'Our first step is a success! The Waygate does indeed work.'

nodes.name: The Exile discovers the Well of Souls
nodes.summary: In Act 2 the Exile follows Abyssal fissures into the Lightless Passage; the Hooded One teaches them the Abyssal tongue and names Kulemak.

nodes.name: Whakapanu Island (PoE2 quest)
nodes.summary: Required Act 4 side quest, begun by speaking to Makoru and sailing to Whakapanu Island; the Exile enters the Singing Caverns and kills the Siren Diamora. Part of the rotating Act 4 requirements.
sources: Infobox (required: Yes, act 4, start 'Sailing to Whakapanu Island', completion 'Defeat Diamora, Song of Death'); quest log '===Enter the Singing Caverns===' to '===Kill Diamora==='

nodes.name: Precursor Cataclysm
nodes.summary: After mastering corruption the Precursors delved into world secrets, triggering great fires, eruptions and impacts from the sky; the civilisation was wiped out by an unknown cataclysm. Cause unclear.

nodes.name: Priesthood conspiracy (stabbing of Olroth)
nodes.summary: High Priest Uhtred, suspecting Olroth of fighting for the horrors in his sleep, had a dozen priests stab him (71 wounds); Vorana killed all twelve; Olroth was encased in glass and Uhtred fled to an ancient site of power.

nodes.name: Purity Rebellion
nodes.summary: A rebellion led by High Templar Voll and the poet Victario, with King Kaom, Sekhema Deshret and Thane Rigwald. It culminates in the siege of Sarn (Divini, 1334 IC) and Voll's coronation.
sources: sections 'The Purity Rebellion', 'Siege of Sarn', 'Assassination of Chitus'
issues #1-4 (Death to Sin / The Black Heart)

alt_summaries.summary: Voll's crusade against Gemlings.

nodes.name: The Temple Door Idol from the Queen of Filth
nodes.summary: The Exile enters the Drowned City and Aggorat, defeats the Queen of Filth, and takes the Temple Door Idol to open the Temple of Kopec.
sources: Quest 'Defeat the Queen of Filth' / 'Pick up the Temple Door Idol'

nodes.name: Rapture Device activation
nodes.summary: 1336 IC; Dialla refuses; Malachai enters Beast.

nodes.name: Slay the Bloated Miller
nodes.summary: The Exile follows a wounded man's warning to Clearfell, kills the Bloated Miller, and receives a reward from Renly (the quest is on The Riverbank; the Miller attacks the camp).

nodes.name: The Red Communion
nodes.summary: Project that allowed Atziri to commune directly with the Beast. Doryani, privately opposed, was forced to devise it; he learned all he could and prepared contingencies. It triggered the Vaal Cataclysm.
sources: Spymaster note: 'consequences of the Red Communion'

nodes.name: Return of the Sun
nodes.summary: The Winter of the World ends: Maraketh tradition credits twin sekhema Solerai and Lundara expelling the Lightless; official Abyss text credits Solaris. Sources differ (possibly the same figures).
sources: The Lightless final paragraph; The Maraketh

nodes.name: Dispel the sandstorm with the Horn of the Vastiri
nodes.summary: The Exile sounds the Horn of the Vastiri at the sandstorm, dispelling Jamanra's barrier, and Asala then turns the caravan toward Deshar.
sources: Quest 'Use the Horn of the Vastiri' / 'Speak to Asala'

nodes.name: Release the Hooded One from the Tree of Souls
nodes.summary: In the Grelwood the Exile finds the Tree of Souls holding the Hooded One; Una says only runes can break the binding, so the Exile collects Runes of Power from the Red Vale and stabs them into the Tree with the forged Rune Spikes.
sources: Quest 'Use the Rune Spikes' / 'Speak to Una'

nodes.name: Seed of Corruption Released
nodes.summary: About 20 years after Kitava's defeat, Count Geonor pierces the Hooded One with a runic sword and extracts the Seed of Corruption, which begins feeding on a soldier. Corruption spreads across Wraeclast and the Atlas.

nodes.name: Siege of Sarn
nodes.summary: On the last day of Divini 1334 IC, High Templar Voll laid siege to Sarn with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh rebel support. Cadiro Perandus negotiated Sarn's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC, and Voll was crowned a week later.
sources: section 'Siege of Sarn (Divini, 1334 IC)' and the paragraph after 'Assassination of Chitus' (surrender and coronation)

alt_summaries.summary: Divini 1334 IC; Voll besieges Sarn.

nodes.name: Sin Consults Kalandra
nodes.summary: Sin seeks Kalandra at her lake and receives cryptic instructions leading him to a Precursor ruin holding the Seed of Corruption, used to create the Beast. Etching V's 'little thief' is read as Sin; PoE1 link is inference, PoE2 wiki states it directly.

nodes.name: Slumber of the Gods
nodes.summary: Sin plants the Dark Ember in Highgate, creating the Beast, the source of thaumaturgy. The Beast initiates the Slumber of the Gods, which puts all gods to sleep.

nodes.name: Slumbering of the Gods
nodes.summary: Sin's Beast lulled the gods into dreamless slumber, ending an era of divine strife; Hinekora foresaw it and prepared the Halls of the Dead before sleeping.

chronology.relative: unknown, millennia before PoE1 (before the Vaal Empire per PoE2 wiki)

sources: Sin 'The Rise of the Gods': "We gods, we were driven into slumbering darkness, to dream away eternity whilst the gentle Beast watched over us."
Hinekora dream: 'She foresaw the Slumbering of the Gods' / hinekora wiki Lore

nodes.name: Open the Memorial Gate for Lachlann
nodes.summary: In the Cemetery of the Eternals the Exile destroys Asinia and Praetor Draven for the two Memorial Key pieces, opens the gate, and puts Lachlann to rest.

nodes.name: Templars shift to Oriath
nodes.summary: After the Cataclysm.

nodes.name: Templar Theocracy of Oriath
nodes.summary: After the Cataclysm, the Templars shift their base to Oriath and develop a theocracy. The Templar Courts and Chamber of Innocence are built under High Templar Avarius shortly before PoE1.

nodes.name: Defeat Ketzuli in the Temple of Kopec
nodes.summary: In the Temple of Kopec the Exile defeats Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun, and Alva activates an elevator and gateway into the Ziggurat's past.
sources: Quest 'Defeat Ketzuli, High Priest of the Sun' / 'Ride the Elevator'

nodes.name: Revive the Hooded One with Count Lachlann's ring
nodes.summary: Through the Grim Tangle, the Exile brings Count Lachlann's ring to Una, who revives the Hooded One; he reveals the Seed of Corruption is in Ogham and must be recovered.
sources: Quest 'Witness the revival of the Hooded One'

nodes.name: Mastodon Tusks from the Bone Pits
nodes.summary: In the Bone Pits the Exile defeats Ekbab and Iktab for the Mastodon Tusks that Jamanra wanted for lightning powers.
sources: Walkthrough 'Defeat Ekbab, Ancient Steed and Iktab'

nodes.name: Enter the time gateway to Utzaal's past
nodes.summary: The gateway sends the Exile and Alva into Utzaal's past, where the Vaal see Alva and the Exile as threats while the Cataclysm is imminent.
sources: Quest 'Enter the Time Portal' / 'Enter Utzaal in the past'

nodes.name: Titans and Humans Fight the Rising Darkness
nodes.summary: A 'rising darkness' (likely the Lightless after the Winter of the World) attacks Titans and humans; surviving Titans forge weapons and unearth the first virtue gem, but are almost wiped out.

nodes.name: Defeat Tor Gul in the Spires of Deshar
nodes.summary: In Deshar the Exile climbs the Path of Mourning to the Spires, where the Faridun have taken the honoured dead, and defeats Tor Gul, the Defiler.

nodes.name: Kill the Executioner and free Leitis
nodes.summary: The Exile finds the Executioner at Ogham Village, frees his prisoner Leitis, and Leitis (who says 'He killed Eamon') then asks the Exile to depose Count Geonor.

nodes.name: Merchant Wars and War of the Great Families
nodes.summary: Feud between House Keita and House Bardiya that escalated into civil war and ended in a ceasefire and the Merchant Council.

nodes.name: Trarthan Rebellion against Phrecius (870 IC)
nodes.summary: Warlords of Trarthus were executed after Phrecian legions occupied it; four first-generation Trarthans led a war; Karui blockades and Ezomyte sabotage doomed reinforcements; Tyndarus capitulated after two years.

nodes.name: Trarthan War of Independence
nodes.summary: 870-872 IC rebellion against Tyndarus.

nodes.name: Trial of the Ancestors
nodes.summary: Tournament in the Halls of the Dead where the Exile's team of Karui warriors fights teams led by the ten Karui chieftains, destroying totems; winning a full tournament earns rewards from Hinekora (omens, Hinekora's Lock, unique items).
sources: 'rules over the Halls of the Dead and oversees the Trial of the Ancestors'

nodes.name: Trials of Chaos
nodes.summary: Escalating wave trials in which a Trialmaster-set modifier is added each round; the player banks or risks rewards. PoE1 Ultimatum league (3.14), core in 3.23; PoE2 Ascension Trial of Chaos (Act 3 Temple of Chaos, up to 10 trials).

nodes.name: Loss of the Triskelion Flame
nodes.summary: The starlight barrier vanished as Vorana tried to adjust it; the Flame's altar was empty and all harbour ships but one had been burned. Vorana branded Uhtred a traitor, and Olroth's glass case was found empty. Uhtred had fled to an ancient shrine.

nodes.name: Twilight Order rebuilds Oriath
nodes.summary: After the abandonment, the Twilight Order emerged from secrecy and rebuilt Oriath in secret; Act 5 is set there and the Beast is held there (per Kanu).
sources: intro: 'Oriath, which was rebuilt in secret'

nodes.name: Survive the Utzaal Cataclysm through the gateway
nodes.summary: The Exile and Alva survive the Cataclysm in Utzaal's past and return through the gateway with Doryani, who then laments that his people are long dead.

alt_summaries.summary: Doryani, Alva and the Exile use the gateway as the Cataclysm begins ('It begins...'); they return to the present where Doryani sees Utzaal as a grave.

nodes.name: Vaal first contact with the Azmeri
nodes.summary: Around 1160 BC (Trinian, writing c. 1333 IC, says about 2,500 years earlier) the Vaal first contacted the primitive Azmeri tribes of the Azmerian ranges, introducing agriculture and literacy and helping create the first Azmerian written language, while never divulging the secret of virtue gems.

chronology.relative: c. 1160 BC (~2,500 years before Chitus, per Trinian)

sources: section 'Contacting the Azmeri'; Trinian, The Ancients Book 4

nodes.name: Vaal Cataclysm
