nodes.summary: Event c. 400 BIC that ended the Vaal Empire: Doryani's project to grant immortality (manipulating the Beast, corruption, gems, sacrifice and 'communion') went wrong; only 3,126 Vaal survived and took refuge with the Azmeri. PoE2 shows the Red Communion and Atziri being swallowed by the Beast.
sources: section 'The Vaal Cataclysm' (paragraph on Path of Exile 2: Fate of the Vaal)
Abilities: 'cutscene... swallowed by the Beast and starting the Cataclysm'

alt_summaries.summary: Doryani's attempt at immortality under Queen Atziri destroys the Vaal Empire. Only 3,126 Vaal survive, and they are absorbed into the Azmeri. In PoE2's Fate of the Vaal league the Exile travels back in time, with Doryani's help, to the moment before the Cataclysm.

nodes.name: Survivors among the Azmeri
nodes.summary: The 3,126 surviving Vaal found refuge among the Azmeri, could not explain what happened, had no gems and assimilated until none remained; they panicked at an image of a gem shown by the Kalguur.

nodes.name: Vastiri Becomes a Desert
nodes.summary: Over thousands of years the plains' rivers dried and forests became sand, naturally or via Maraketh/Halani-linked causes; the Maraketh became semi-nomadic.

nodes.name: Defeat Viper Napuatzi in Utzaal's past
nodes.summary: In Utzaal's past the Vaal general Viper Napuatzi has Alva taken to Doryani; the Exile defeats Napuatzi to open the path.

nodes.name: Ban on collecting virtue gems in Kalguur
nodes.summary: After the Azmeri reacted fearfully to virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third officially banned their collection; the gems never returned to Kalguur (Kalguur page, Thaumaturgy section).

chronology.relative: during the reign of Cadigan III (ancient Kalguur)

sources: ===Thaumaturgy===: "after witnessing the Azmeris' fearful reaction towards virtue gems, King Cadigan the Third had officially banned their collection"

nodes.name: Voll crowned Emperor
nodes.summary: Voll of Thebrus crowned Emperor in Sacrato of Phreci 1334 IC (Eternal Empire page: a week after Cadiro's surrender on 1 Sacrato of Phreci; Purity Chronicles Book 1 says the 2nd Sacrato of Phreci).

nodes.name: Voll's pact with Deshret
nodes.summary: Voll promises Sekhema Deshret the return of the Vastiri Plains for Maraketh support; she demands Titucius' skin for a saddle.

nodes.name: Voll's pact with Kaom
nodes.summary: Voll and Victario visit Kaom in Ngamakanui; Voll promises Karui sovereignty over Wraeclast's south shore and freedom for slaves in exchange for attacking Lioneye's Watch.

nodes.name: Winter of the World
aliases: Winter of the World (Great Fire / Great Wasting)
nodes.summary: Ancient war in which Kulemak and the Lightless blanketed the Vastiri Plains and the surface, ended when the Three Sisters (Solerai/Lundara etc.) destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and brought back the sun.
sources: paragraph 1: 'Winter of the World ... lasted for centuries'
Great Fire: 'revealed that the Great Fire was indeed the same event as the Winter of the World'

alt_summaries.summary: Volcanic eruptions fill the sky with ash. The Lightless attack destroys the primeval civilization, fells the Titans and devastates the Maraketh and Azmeri. The Order of the Djinn later defeats the Lightless.
Initial Abyssal (Lightless) invasion of the surface, ended by the Three Sisters who destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and brought back the sun. Minimal node; fuller entry owned by another domain.
Ancient cataclysm of ash, fire and Lightless invasion; PoE2 confirmed the Ezomyte Great Fire is the same event. PoE1 wiki says it was likely caused by the Fourth Edict.

nodes.name: Defeat Xyclucian and enter the Machinarium
nodes.summary: In the Chimeral Wetlands the Exile defeats Xyclucian, the Chimera, and enters Jiquani's Machinarium, where Alva sends them after a small Soul Core.
sources: Quest 'Defeat Xyclucian, the Chimera' / 'Enter Jiquani's Machinarium'

nodes.name: Doryani's investigation of Zerphi
nodes.summary: Atziri ordered Doryani to research Zerphi's rejuvenation 'within the realms of possibility... without fear of question or consequence'; Vaal aged 16-26 were sent to him and none survived, the experiments failing.

nodes.name: Defeat Zicoatl and take the large Soul Core
nodes.summary: Inside Jiquani's Sanctum the Exile powers two generators with medium Soul Cores and defeats Zicoatl, Warden of the Core, to take the large Soul Core.
sources: Quest 'Activate two Generators' / 'Defeat Zicoatl, Warden of the Core'

nodes.name: Arrive at the Ziggurat Encampment in Utzaal
nodes.summary: The Hooded One sends the Exile to Utzaal; the Exile crosses the Sandswept Marsh to the Ziggurat, meeting Oswald and Alva.

nodes.name: The Afarud
nodes.summary: Rogue Faridun sect that torments djinn; led by figures such as Ridan, Afarud Commander.

alt_summaries.summary: Outcasts of the Faridun who use forbidden rites and seek destruction of Maraketh and Faridun alike, led by Saresh.

nodes.name: Ardura Akhara
nodes.summary: Maraketh akhara (caravan order) led by Sekhema Asala and Zarka that the Exile joins in Act 2.

nodes.name: Azmeri
nodes.summary: Ancient tribal people of the Azmerian ranges who worship Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi and others. Eighty thousand of them under Tarcus Veruso descended into the former Vaal lands and founded the Eternal Empire in 1 IC; the Azmeri of the Forest Encampment and the Wildwood descend from those who stayed behind.

alt_summaries.summary: One of the oldest peoples of Wraeclast from the Azmerian Ranges; first lettered by the Vaal, worshipped Solaris, Lunaris, Viridi; their migrants founded the Eternal Empire (only pre-1 IC history counts as 'Azmerian'); Maji remnants in the Wildwood.
Wildwood people.
Tribal people of the Azmerian ranges who took in the Vaal survivors.

nodes.name: Black Scythe
nodes.summary: Kalguuran mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana, responsible for the expedition's defence and offence. Their artifacts are the currency of the Expedition NPC Tujen.

alt_summaries.summary: Mercenaries (mostly crossbow arbalists) led by Vorana.

nodes.name: Black Scythes
nodes.summary: Kalguuran mercenaries led by Vorana, fighting horrors from walls with crossbows.

nodes.name: The Caaltu
nodes.summary: A civilisation that existed in Kahuturoa's time (Vastiri still forest, Vaal extant, Oriath recently founded, Ezomyr not yet struck by plague) and was only a memory by Maata's time. Little else is known.

nodes.name: The Cuachic
nodes.summary: Isolated Vaal remnant in Mount Kriar's vault, living under strict control for generations; recruited by Doryani's phrase in PoE2 Interlude.

alt_summaries.summary: Sealed Vaal remnant under Mount Kriar loyal to Doryani; The Hooded One warns the pact lasts only while there is a common enemy.

nodes.name: Druids of Skothe
nodes.summary: Ancient order that venerated the Azmeri Draiocht and practised the mystic arts of the Maji; the Druid (an Ezomyte) was once a member. Wiped out by the King in the Mists and his cultists, who deceived them by disguising himself as a Maji of the old.
sources: page 'Lore': 'The Druid is an Ezomyte who was once part of the Druids of Skothe, an ancient order that venerated the Azmeri Draíocht and practiced the mystic arts of the Maji.'

nodes.name: Druids of the Broken Circle
nodes.summary: Kalguuran nature-mystics under Medved, named after Olroth's gem use clouded their scrying.

alt_summaries.summary: Nature-mystics led by Medved; PoE2 names Gronel Starseer, Smalon Thickett, Avon Bruhn.
Kalguuran nature-mystic sect led by Medved, who could see the future by 'peering into the past'. Medved lost that sight the night Olroth set out alone with a gem.

nodes.name: Eternal Empire
nodes.summary: Oriathan/imperial civilisation, also called the Sarn Empire, founded in 1 IC by Azmeri migrants under Tarcus Veruso on the ruins of the Vaal capital. Ruled by Emperors from Sarn, it held most of central Wraeclast with a Roman-style legion system until the Cataclysm (c. 1339 IC) destroyed it; Oriath survived as its successor.

chronology.relative: 1 IC to c. 1339 IC; roughly 260 years before PoE1 (1599-1600 IC)

sources: lead paragraph and sections 'History' through 'The Cataclysm'
Act 1: Cemetery of the Eternals / Eternal prison areas

alt_summaries.summary: The Sarn-based Eternal Empire founded by Tarcus Veruso at 1 IC and ruled by Emperors from Sarn. The Cataclysm around 1339 IC ended it.
Old Empire of Wraeclast.

nodes.name: Ezomytes
nodes.summary: Clan people of Ezomyr, subjugated and enslaved by the Eternal Empire. Thane Rigwald rallied them in the Bloody Flowers Rebellion of 1333 IC and they joined the siege of Sarn.

alt_summaries.summary: People of Ezomyr and the Isles of Skothe who worship the First Ones; Ezomyr was later largely wiped by plague; speak Ezo.

nodes.name: Faridun
nodes.summary: Maraketh rejects (flawed or mutated newborns left in the dunes) raised by wandering Faridun tribes in the Vastiri, who accept necromancy and long for reunification with the akharas. In PoE2 Act 2 the Countess recruits them with the promise of resurrecting Jamanra.
sources: Overview and Events in Path of Exile 2

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh outcasts left to die in the Vastiri, resentful and necromancy-dabbling; antagonists in PoE2 Act 2.
Desert people of Vastiri set against the Maraketh; featured in PoE2 as well.
Rejected Maraketh outcasts of the Vastiri desert, who ally with the Countess and resurrected Jamanra to feed the Beast.
Faridun sect led by Prince Azmadi, allied with the Serpent Clan avenging Keth's queen.

nodes.name: Gemling Legion
nodes.summary: Elite legions of the Eternal Empire created by Malachai: legionnaires infused with virtue gems, led by Captains, which gave the Empire military dominance. Chitus carried a master gem whose heartbeat bound every gemling to his own, so they fell when he died; survivors were transformed by the Cataclysm into the Undying.

nodes.name: The Godless Three
nodes.summary: Three thaumaturgists trained by Malachai: Shavronne of Umbra, Maligaro the Inquisitor and Doedre Darktongue. Maligaro and Doedre were burned by Voll; Malachai later revived all three to guard his heart, lungs and entrails.

alt_summaries.summary: Malachai's three most loyal servants: Maligaro, Shavronne, Doedre, guarding his organs.

nodes.name: House Azadi
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Contract-assassin monopoly.

nodes.name: House Bardiya
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Financiers; Merchant Council with greatest control today.

nodes.name: House Cyaxan
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Drug trade, criminal syndicate and mass virtue gem implantation.

nodes.name: House Keita
nodes.summary: Trarthan Great House. Slave armies, flesh pits; failed to become a god; founded Korathin 872 IC.

nodes.name: Kalguuran settlers
nodes.summary: Runesmith people of Middengard who built Kingsmarch (Rog, Tujen, Dannig, Gwennen), led by the Cadigan kings; PoE1 Settlers of Kalguur continues into PoE2 Act 4.

alt_summaries.summary: People of Kalguur: rune-smiths who use runes of starlight, have no gods, lack inherent affinity for virtue gems, and live under King Cadigan; settlers in Wraeclast built Kingsmarch.
Seafaring Kalguuran, shown a gem image by Vaal survivors.

nodes.name: Karui
nodes.summary: Seafaring warrior people of the southern archipelago. Under King Kaom they allied with Voll's Purity Rebellion, took Lioneye's Watch and founded the first Karui settlement on the mainland; Kaom later fell at Highgate. The Empire had enslaved Karui under Chitus.

alt_summaries.summary: Nomadic seafaring people of Ngamakanui following the Karui Way; once peaceful farmers and fishermen until Tukohama armed them; ever-changing pantheon; Hinekora made the Halls of the Dead.
Island people of Ngamakanui.

Island people of Ngamakanui (Tukohama, Tasalio, Ngamahu, Tawhoa, Hinekora tribes) who in Act 4 ally with the Exile; ancestors remain in the Halls of the Dead and 'Ngakuramakoi' can be non-Karui by blood.
Island people who obstructed Doryani.

nodes.name: Arohongui tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Arohongui and is led by the chieftain Ikiaho; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Hinekora tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Hinekora and is led by the chieftain Tawhanuku; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Kitava tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Kitava and is led by the chieftain Utula; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Ngamahu tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Ngamahu and is led by the chieftain Kaom; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Ramako tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Ramako and is led by the chieftain Ahuana; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Rongokurai tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Rongokurai and is led by the chieftain Kahuturoa; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Tasalio tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tasalio and is led by the chieftain Rakiata; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Tawhoa tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tawhoa and is led by the chieftain Maata; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Tukohama tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Tukohama and is led by the chieftain Akoya; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Valako tribe
nodes.summary: Karui tribe that honours the Karui Ancestor Valako and is led by the chieftain Kiloava; each tribe offers a unique item in the Trial of the Ancestors.
sources: tribe/chieftain list; 'The Karui tribes are grouped by the Karui Ancestor they currently worship'

nodes.name: Keepers of the Flame (Order of the Purple Flame)
nodes.summary: Monastic order founded by Ailith after her visions of the Dreamer; they train in the Monastery to defend Wraeclast against the Hiveborn and tend the Genesis Tree. The PoE2 wiki calls it the Order of the Purple Flame; the Monk class belongs to it. It is a taboo among them to speak the Dreamer's true name (Chayula).
sources: Visit the Monastery of the Keepers: "Welcome to our Monastery..."

alt_summaries.summary: Cult formed in Chayula's dreams, dedicated to destroying the Hiveborn; based at the Monastery of the Keepers.

nodes.name: Knights of the Sun
nodes.summary: Warriors and military enforcers under direct orders of the King, led by Olroth.

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran martial order led by Olroth who adopted gems on weapons and armour.
Powerful Kalguuran warriors/enforcers directly under the King; led by Olroth; religious scrutiny by them drove some emigration.

nodes.name: The Lightless
nodes.summary: Necromantic army of possessed golems created by Kulemak, led by Abyssal Liches; ended the primeval civilisation.

nodes.name: The Maji
nodes.summary: Azmeri vanguard chosen when the Wildwood was made; they purge the Nameless and fight the King in the Mists, forbidden from touching virtue gems ('Tears of the Maji').

alt_summaries.summary: Azmeri vanguard sent into the Wildwood to wait while it is purged of evil, waging war on the King in the Mists.

nodes.name: Maraketh
nodes.summary: Desert people of the Vastiri led by Sekhemas, living in akhara (tribes). In 1333 IC Sekhema Deshret joined the Purity Rebellion in exchange for the return of the Vastiri Plains; later, Deshret sealed the Highgate mines. A large tribe lives at Highgate in PoE1; the Ardura akhara and Sekhema Asala appear in PoE2.

alt_summaries.summary: Matriarchal people led by sekhema, ancient dwellers of Vastiri for 304 generations; endured the Winter of the World, expelled the Lightless, had a thousand-year golden age at Keth, then lost their gods to the Beast's slumber and drifted into the desert.
Desert nomads of the Vastiri.
Desert people of the Vastiri; the Ardura akhara and the honoured dead of Deshar are Maraketh.

nodes.name: Meridian Free Traders
nodes.summary: Trade guild that sent Raulf to assist executing the Kingsmarch charter; in PoE2 it controls boat charters (Makoru captains the Aurora May under it).

alt_summaries.summary: Kingsmarch guild under which Makoru's Aurora May works; requires an account and charter from Rog.

nodes.name: House Phrecia (Necropolis dead)
nodes.summary: One of five Eternal Empire-era families whose haunted dead (four members each) can be buried in the Necropolis to grave-craft the unique 'The Hand of Phrecia'.

nodes.name: Order of the Chalice
nodes.summary: Kalguuran priesthood (Priests of the Chalice) that interpreted the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes; Uhtred was its High Priest.

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran priesthood led by Uhtred; found the ancient artefact at the shrine.

nodes.name: Order of the Djinn
nodes.summary: Secret society founded in ancient times by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper (Ahkeli) that protects Wraeclast from calamity and guards dangerous artefacts (Forbidden Vaults near the Oasis, Act 9); takes one orphan from each culture. Members forged and delivered the Starforge to the Watchers of Decay (video). Janus Perandus's betrayal let Catarina raid the vault and the Order was slain except Jun and Janus; in PoE2 Jun is rebuilding it. Past members include Ixchel (later the Trialmaster).
sources: 1:07 order of the Djinn; 16:34 Starforge; 20:10 infiltration of Forbidden Vault

alt_summaries.summary: Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper to protect Wraeclast from calamity and guard dangerous artefacts. Icius Perandus and, much later, Janus Perandus belonged to it.
Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper to protect Wraeclast from calamities; Jun is rebuilding it in PoE2.

Secret society founded by the Maraketh and the Clayshaper that guards dangerous artefacts and prevents calamities; selects one orphan from each culture. Members include Jun, Janus Perandus, Saresh, Ixchel, Dhunan, Sumei (investigated Kalandra's duplication of artefacts). Jun is rebuilding it in PoE2.
Secret order (Jado's) replenishing its ranks; Jado confirms they infiltrated the Sel Khari and will be in Oriath.
Secret order founded by the Maraketh to guard relics and protect Wraeclast; nearly destroyed by Janus's betrayal in PoE1's Betrayal; Jun rebuilds it in secret, per PoE2.

nodes.name: Perandus family
nodes.summary: Wealthiest merchant-lender family of the Eternal Empire (motto 'With piety and justice'). Blocked from the throne by the Phrecians, they rigged Izaro's Labyrinth so Chitus Perandus won; Cadiro looted the treasury before the fall. Descendants include Syndicate member Janus Perandus.
sources: forum announcement describing Cadiro's stolen treasury and indebted dead

alt_summaries.summary: Wealthy and powerful Eternal Empire family that put Malachai in place; basis for the Perandus league treasures.

nodes.name: Phrecian dynasty
nodes.summary: Unbroken line of emperors descended from Alano Phrecia, who founded the line after killing the 'dark being' in 35 IC. It ran from Alano through Romira and Tyndarus to Izaro, who was childless.
sources: sections 'Reign of Alano Phrecia' to 'Reign of Izaro'

nodes.name: Precursors
nodes.summary: Technologically superior ancient civilisation that wholly predates the Winter of the World; mastered corruption, built the Towers (terraforming), the Precursor Weapon and the Arbiter of Ash, then triggered cataclysms of fire, eruptions and sky-impacts. Pictographs read 'Death lies within'.

chronology.relative: further before the Vaal than the Vaal are before the present

nodes.name: Priests of the Chalice
nodes.summary: Religious order that read the stars and mastered alchemy, machinery and runes.

nodes.name: Primeval Civilization ("Proto-Vaal")
nodes.summary: Ancient civilisation preceding the Vaal, unearthed in the Azurite Mine; the name "Proto-Vaal" is an internal term never used in-game and no link to the Vaal is established.

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient culture (internally called 'Proto-Vaal') buried beneath Vaal and Lightless ruins in the Azurite Mines, known from glyphs; First King Uzaza, tyrant Putembo, last king Aul. No proven link to the Vaal.

nodes.name: Purity Rebellion
nodes.summary: Coalition led by High Templar Voll of Thebrus against Chitus' gem-and-thaumaturgy 'thaumatocracy'. Its supporters included Victario, Ondar, Geofri, Kastov and Adus, with Ezomyte, Karui and Maraketh allies.

nodes.name: Redblades
nodes.summary: Human tribe descended from those who settled the Titans' volcanoes; they ritually sacrifice humans to the Molten One, possibly because a Titan destroyed an outpost of El'Abin.

nodes.name: Remembrancers
nodes.summary: Kalguuran scribes who documented the explorations; the Prime Remembrancer's logbooks tell the expedition's fall.

alt_summaries.summary: Documentarians of Kalguuran explorations.

nodes.name: Runefathers
nodes.summary: Aldur's chosen apprentices and artisans of runesmithing; forged the Triskelion Flame to reunite fractured Middengard.
sources: ===The Triskelion Flame===: "After Aldur had passed away, the Runefathers gathered to forge the Triskelion Flame."

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran runesmiths who gathered after Aldur's death to forge the Triskelion Flame in his honour.

nodes.name: Order of the Templar
nodes.summary: Theocratic order led by a High Templar that worships Innocence. Within the Eternal Empire it produced figures such as High Templars Andronicus and Voll; after the Cataclysm it governed the unaffected island of Oriath as the Templar Theocracy, with Dominus and Avarius as its PoE1-era High Templars.

alt_summaries.summary: A human faction led by a High Templar, governing the theocracy of Oriath in the name of Innocence. Its members include High Templars Dominus, Voll and Avarius.
Theocratic order ruling Oriath.

nodes.name: The Unblinking Eye
nodes.summary: Mysterious group associated with the Templars involved in notable events in Wraeclast's history.

nodes.name: The Three Sisters
nodes.summary: Cross-cultural myth of the sun, moon and earth sisters who destroyed Kulemak's mortal form and ended the Winter of the World; named differently by Eternals, Maraketh, Karui, Azmeri and the Wildwood Draiocht (Catha, Mhacha, Morrigan).

alt_summaries.summary: Sun, Moon (and Earth) sisters/gods named differently per culture who ended the Winter of the World by destroying Kulemak's mortal form. Minimal node; owned by another domain.

nodes.name: Trarthans
nodes.summary: People of Trarthus descended from Eternal Empire exiles and slaves, led by four Great Houses.

nodes.name: The Twilight Order
nodes.summary: Secret order, concealed for countless centuries, that rebuilt Oriath while the world believed it abandoned. It aims to free mankind from the 'tyranny of the gods' and build a god-free 'Utopia'; behind the scenes it is plotting to create a new Beast and trigger another Cataclysm. Led by the Countess (Oriana).

chronology.relative: Hidden for centuries; active ~20 years after the end of PoE1 (PoE1 present is ~1620 IC)

sources: intro quote (Path of Exile 2 Art Book): 'The Twilight Order, however, did not flee. They emerged from countless centuries of secrecy to rebuild Oriath's heart'
intro: 'leader of the Twilight Order... plotting to create a new Beast and start another Cataclysm'
Confront Kanu and the First Herald: Countess 'The Twilight Order will see to it that the world is remade. A world without gods... without suffering... without the disease of Divinity.'

alt_summaries.summary: Cult led by the Countess (Oriana) seeking a 'Utopia' free of the gods, plotting a new Beast and Cataclysm.

nodes.name: The Vaal
nodes.summary: Oldest identified civilisation of Wraeclast and in its heyday its most powerful nation; first known users of virtue gems, practitioners of mass blood sacrifice and slavery. All but 3,126 died in the Vaal Cataclysm; survivors assimilated into the Azmeri.

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient Vaal civilisation.
Vaal civilisation of Utzaal and its remnants; Alva is a descendant of Vaal survivors.

nodes.name: The Royal Architects of Atzoatl
nodes.summary: Group of Vaal architects serving Atziri who built the Temple; Incursion has Vaal Architect mini-bosses. PoE2 Medallion flavour names Architects of the Guild, Vault, Destruction, Hoard, Forge and Nexus and associates Quipolatl, Puhuarte, Juatalotli, Hayoxi, Estazunti with them.

nodes.name: Vaal survivors / Savage tribes heirs
nodes.summary: The 3,126 survivors who merged into Azmeri tribes; later Azmeri/Karui cultures inherit Vaal remnants. Descendants of Vaal blood persist (e.g. Alva Valai; the Cuachic).
sources: Doryani: 'a living descendant of our people'

nodes.name: Watchers of Decay
nodes.summary: Ancient organisation of parents founded when a nameless god told an Azmeri mother whose child was stolen about the Elder. They forged Starforge to subdue it by separating form and spirit. Their Map Device (Book of Memories p9) later became the Atlas device. Associated with the Order of the Djinn on the wiki; membership of Egrin/Qianga/Betucia is unclear.

nodes.name: Abyss league
nodes.summary: Abyss league Launched 2017-12-08 (version 3.1.0). Abysses are cracks and pits spawning monsters; introduces abyss jewels, Stygian Vises, Abyssal Depths and Abyssal Liches.

nodes.name: Dawn of the Hunt
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access update 0.2.0 (launched 2025-04-04) and its temporary league. It added Azmeri wisps, rogue exiles and idols to the core game; not officially a full league.
sources: lead: launched April 4, 2025 as part of Path of Exile 2: Dawn of the Hunt, version 0.2.0; ended August 26, 2025

nodes.name: Fate of the Vaal
nodes.summary: 0.4.0 temporary league centred on Atziri's Temple (Lira Vaal): Ancient Beacons, the Temple Console, Royal Architect Xipocado and Queen Atziri; later moved into the core game (see 0.5 'Fate of the Vaal moving to core').

alt_summaries.summary: PoE2 0.4.0 league (12 Dec 2025 - 25 May 2026) introducing Ancient Beacons, Atziri's Temple and the Red Queen; part of The Last of the Druids.

nodes.name: Forbidden Rites league (PoE2)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access event league (0.5.5, 2026-09-04) built on Ritual altars in campaign and endgame zones, with unique-boss Ritual clusters per act and Sacred Bloom Wildwood encounters; 0.5.5 also integrates Runes of Aldur and Expedition into the core PoE2 game.
sources: lead, 'League content' and unique boss rituals

alt_summaries.summary: 0.5.5 event league (2026-09-04) running beside Runes of Aldur: Ritual encounters in every campaign and endgame zone, unique-boss Ritual clusters per act, Viridian Wildwood via Sacred Bloom; integrates Runes of Aldur and Expedition into core.

nodes.name: Return of the Ancients / Runes of Aldur (0.5.0)
nodes.summary: 0.5.0 expansion (2026-05-29) adding the Legacy of the Precursors endgame story (Arbiter of Ash, Origin Tower, Arbiter of Divinity) and the Runes of Aldur league (Farrow, Verisium, Kalguuran runes). Runes of Aldur is expected to end before the 1.0 release.
sources: lead: launched May 29, 2026 as part of Path of Exile 2: Return of the Ancients, version 0.5.0

alt_summaries.summary: PoE2 update 0.5.0 (2026-05-29), final major pre-1.0 patch: rebuilt Atlas with fixed storylines, Precursor Fortress, Atlas Masters, Runes of Aldur league, Spirit Walker and Martial Artist ascendancies.

nodes.name: Rise of the Abyssal
nodes.summary: First 'full' PoE2 league (0.3.0, 2025-08-29 to 2025-12-09): Abyssal fissures open as green cracks near monster packs; closing them reveals an Abyssal Trove and sometimes the Abyssal Depths; preserved bones feed desecration at the Well of Souls (Act 2).

alt_summaries.summary: Challenge league launched 2025-08-29 with The Third Edict (v0.3.0), the release that added Act 4, the Interludes and Abyss content.
First PoE2 full league, launched 2025-08-29 with version 0.3.0 (The Third Edict); Abysses, preserved bones, the Well of Souls (Act 2) and desecrated modifiers.

nodes.name: Runes of Aldur
nodes.summary: 0.5.0 temporary league: Farrow studies runes on Verisium Remnants (Ezomyte Runesmithing with Kalguuran origins), producing Runic Ward, Kalguuran gems and alloys; folded into the core game with Expedition in 0.5.5.
sources: Runes of Aldur (Runesmithing): Farrow, a young blacksmith, reveals the Kalguuran origins of Ezomyte Runesmithing

alt_summaries.summary: PoE2 Early Access temporary league (0.5.0 'Return of the Ancients', 2026-05-29) in which Farrow studies runes on Verisium Remnants; brings Kalguuran runesmithing, Ward and Kalguuran gems to PoE2.

nodes.name: The Last of the Druids (0.4.0)
aliases: The Last of the Druids / Fate of the Vaal (0.4.0)
nodes.summary: PoE2 Early Access update 0.4.0 (2025-12-12): added the Druid class, the Fate of the Vaal league, many support gems and endgame changes.
sources: released December 12, 2025 with Druid class and Fate of the Vaal league
lead: launched December 12, 2025 as part of The Last of the Druids, version 0.4.0

alt_summaries.summary: 0.4.0 expansion (2025-12-12) with the Fate of the Vaal league (Atziri's Temple); background to Doryani/Vaal threads continuing into the endgame.

nodes.name: Path of Exile 2: The Third Edict (0.3.0)
nodes.summary: Content update launching Aug 29, 2025: Act 4 (Ngamakanui), three interludes, removal of Cruel, and Rise of the Abyssal league; named after the Weapon's Third Edict.
sources: Act Four continues from Act 3 ... Doryani agrees to help find an ancient weapon, the instrument of the Third Edict; three Interludes lead to level 65 where endgame begins; Cruel removed
intro: launched August 29, 2025 as part of The Third Edict (0.3.0)

alt_summaries.summary: PoE2 Early Access update 0.3.0 (2025-08-29): added Act 4 (Kingsmarch, Ngamakanui, hunt for the Weapon/instrument of the Third Edict), three Interludes, removal of Cruel difficulty, and Rise of the Abyssal league.

nodes.name: Abandoned Prison / Solitary Confinement
nodes.summary: Eternal Empire prison island; staff fed prisoners their own regrowing flesh after the Cataclysm (Tattered Diary). Solitary Confinement holds The Prisoner, sealed by Emperor Chitus under an order from Izaro.

nodes.name: Abyssal Depths
nodes.summary: Areas reached from Abysses containing Abyssal monsters and lich bosses Amanamu and Ulaman.

nodes.name: Aggorat
nodes.summary: Opulent Vaal district of Utzaal, known for golden tributes at its main temple's apex; in the past it holds the Black Chambers where Doryani keeps Alva. In the present the Exile reaches it via the Drowned City and the Apex of Filth, defeating the Queen of Filth for the Temple Door Idol.

alt_summaries.summary: Vaal structure known as the Apex of Filth, beyond the Drowned City; holds the Queen of Filth and the Black Chambers.

nodes.name: Ancient Gateway
aliases: Ancient Gateway and the Fortress Gateways
nodes.summary: Precursor gateway site the Exile reaches in Legacy of the Precursors after the Precursor Fortress rises; the Exile uses its levers and a Precursor Beacon there to open the route to the Burning Monolith.
sources: quest log: 'Travel to the Ancient Gateway', 'Explore the Ancient Gateway', 'Find and use Levers', 'Activate the Precursor Beacon'

nodes.name: Arastas
nodes.summary: Karui-archipelago island in Act 4 where the Twilight Order's church and Torvian are found; the Excavation lies beyond.

nodes.name: The Ardura Caravan
nodes.summary: Mobile Maraketh caravan and Act 2 town hub, led by Zarka and Sekhema Asala.

nodes.name: Atziri's Temple (Lira Vaal)
nodes.summary: Past version of the temple unlocked via Ancient Beacons; the present ruin is the Lost Temple. Built via the Temple Console; Doryani turns the entrance into a time portal after Act 3/4.
sources: lead; Ancient Beacon; Doryani will activate the time portal

nodes.name: Aul's Domain (Crystal King's Throne)
nodes.summary: Delve area (internally 'Proto-Vaal city') of the Azurite Mine where the crystal-encased citadel and throne of Aul, the Crystal King, lie.
sources: Primeval civilization; footnote: 'Proto-Vaal' is the internal name of Delve's Primeval Chamber and The Crystal King's Throne

alt_summaries.summary: Delve node (Primeval Ruins biome) containing the Primeval Citadel where Aul is fought.

nodes.name: Axiom Prison
nodes.summary: Ancient clifftop prison (no one remembers who built it) used by every power that ruled Wraeclast; its warden Brutus was mutated; Act 1 area from Lower Prison to Warden's Chambers.
sources: Shavronne in her tower in the Prison

alt_summaries.summary: Eternal outpost warded by Brutus where Shavronne of Umbra experimented on him; blocked Karui advance.
Prison complex reached through the Act 6 Ridge; contains Shavronne's Tower, where Shavronne's spirit is killed for Sin.

nodes.name: The Azak Bog
nodes.summary: Act 3 swamp area where the Azak tribe lives; site of Ignagduk's arena at Gor-gor Mog and the start of the Tribal Vengeance quest.
sources: Lead: 'a quest in the act 3 area The Azak Bog'; 'Start' field

nodes.name: Azala Vaal
nodes.summary: Vaal capital named after the burning of Lira Vaal's temple; now buried beneath Sarn where the Azmeri founded the Eternal Empire's capital.

alt_summaries.summary: Former capital of the Vaal Empire; Tarcus Veruso planted his banner here to found Sarn and the Eternal Empire.

nodes.name: Viridian Wildwood
nodes.summary: Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons there, the Maji fight the Nameless and the King in the Mists. PoE2 Last of the Druids setting.
sources: The Winter of the World > The Viridian Wildwood
paragraph on the forest not existing until 3.23.0

alt_summaries.summary: Haven created by the Draiocht as refuge from the Winter of the World; time loops in seasons; haunted by shadowy creatures such as the King in the Mists; home of the Maji.

Refuge created by the Draiocht against the Winter of the World, where time loops in seasons. Contested by the Nameless and the King in the Mists; Chaos believes the forest did not exist until the 3.23 timeline.
Wildwood encounter on the Atlas, connected to Sacred Bloom rewards; Aoife is bound here.

nodes.name: Azmerian Ranges
nodes.summary: Mountain homeland of the ancient Azmeri; origin of the migrants who founded Sarn and the Eternal Empire, and where the Vaal first met the Azmeri.

nodes.name: The Black Chambers
nodes.summary: Complex within Aggorat where Doryani keeps Alva in the past of Utzaal; Act 3 boss area where the Exile captures Doryani (act boss: Doryani, Royal Thaumaturge).
sources: Quest log 'Find Doryani in the Black Chambers'

alt_summaries.summary: Chambers in Aggorat where Doryani is found holding Alva.

nodes.name: The Bone Pits
nodes.summary: Site in the Mastodon Badlands where Ekbab and Iktab guard the Mastodon Tusks.

nodes.name: Buried Shrines
nodes.summary: Shrine area of Keth guarded by Azarian, the Forsaken Son.

nodes.name: Caer Tarth
nodes.summary: Ritual hub on the 0.5 Atlas, west of the starting point.

nodes.name: Cemetery of the Eternals
nodes.summary: PoE2 Act 1 area in Ogham where Eternal praetors are entombed, with inscriptions claiming the land 'in life and death'.

alt_summaries.summary: Act 1 graveyard hosting the Tomb of the Consort and the Mausoleum of the Praetor.

nodes.name: Chamber of Innocence
nodes.summary: Templar chamber in Oriath built under High Templar Avarius whose stained glass windows tell the Sin and Innocence story.

alt_summaries.summary: Chamber where Avarius becomes Innocence.

nodes.name: Chamber of Sins
nodes.summary: Laboratory built by Chitus where Maligaro conducted flesh experiments, opposed by nearby Phrecia Cathedral; named by Archbishop Geofri.

alt_summaries.summary: Old Empire site where Maligaro worked; holds the Baleful Gem.
Inquisitor Maligaro's laboratory in Phrecia, with a secret passage to the Den.

nodes.name: Chimeral Wetlands
nodes.summary: Wetland crossed on the way to Jiquani's Machinarium, guarded by Xyclucian.

nodes.name: Clearfell
nodes.summary: Ezomyte logging encampment in Ogham that serves as Act 1's town hub, where Una and Renly operate.

nodes.name: Crux of Nothingness
nodes.summary: Atlas site revealed with An Audience with the King where the King in the Mists is fought in the Ritual quest.
sources: steps 14-17 'Reveal the Crux of Nothingness ... Defeat the King in the Mists'

nodes.name: The Crystal Veins
nodes.summary: Highgate caverns holding the Rapture Device, which the exile reactivates to enter the Beast.

alt_summaries.summary: Cave where the Rapture Device stands.

nodes.name: Cuachic Vault
nodes.summary: Isolated vault atop Mount Kriar where a Vaal remnant (Cuachic) lived, controlled and numbed by their High Priests.

nodes.name: Deshar
nodes.summary: Maraketh burial site with the Burial Spires, where the honoured dead are given sky burials.
sources: Quest log 'Use the Desert Map to travel to Deshar'

nodes.name: The Drowned City
nodes.summary: Submerged city section revealed after the lake is drained.

nodes.name: Western and Eastern Enigma Chambers
nodes.summary: Two endgame chambers entered through the Western and Eastern Gateways; each holds a boss fight (Count Geonor in the west, Doryani in the east) and a Crisis Fragment (Ancient and Weathered) needed to open the Burning Monolith.
sources: quest log (hidden comment block): 'Travel to the Western Enigma Chamber', 'Defeat Count Geonor', 'Defeat Doryani', 'Pick up the Ancient Crisis Fragment'
Keys: 'The other two keys can be found in the Western Enigma Chamber and the Eastern Enigma Chamber.'

nodes.name: Eternal Laboratory
nodes.summary: Malachai's laboratory of the Eternal Empire, built on the archbishop Lazhwar's thaumaturgy research into maps; Zana's hideout alternative in the legacy Atlas quests.
sources: Eternal Empire section: 'Lazhwar... discovered maps to create the Eternal Laboratory'
Assignment: 'Talk to Zana in your Hideout or the Eternal Laboratory'

nodes.name: Eye of Hinekora / Halls of the Dead
nodes.summary: Karui afterlife realm unlocked by rescuing Matiki: Tests of Mettle for Kaom, Maata and Rakiata, the Halls of the Dead with Yama's trial and the audience with Hinekora.

alt_summaries.summary: PoE2 Act 4 area accessible after rescuing Matiki; gateway to the Halls of the Dead and Trial of the Ancestors.

nodes.name: Ezomyr
nodes.summary: Ezomyte homeland on a landmass west of the Wraeclastian mainland (with the Isles of Skothe), later largely wiped out by a plague; Ogham forests in PoE2 Act 1.

nodes.name: Forge of the Titans
nodes.summary: Primeval forge reached through Primeval Remnants during Crucible league, where equipment trees are combined; the stone body and voice of the Molten One, the last known Titan, can be met there.
sources: '==League Mechanic==' Primeval Remnant / Forge of the Titans
Molten One entry: 'During Crucible league, his stone body and voice can be encountered in the Forge of the Titans'

alt_summaries.summary: Volcanic caldera (Crucible league) where the Molten One dwells and the Redblades worship him.

nodes.name: The Grim Tangle
nodes.summary: Overgrown sinkholes beneath Ogham leading to the Count's grave past the Memorial Gate.

nodes.name: The Halani Gates
nodes.summary: Gates to the Maraketh city of Deshar; Jamanra locks them; a sandstorm blocks the road after the first battle at the gates.
sources: Quest log 'Talk to Asala about the closed Gates'

nodes.name: The Halls of the Dead
nodes.summary: Karui afterlife created by Hinekora before the Slumbering of the Gods as a place for Karui souls; where fallen chieftains reside and the Trial of the Ancestors is held.
sources: '==Items==' (portal to the Halls of the Dead)

nodes.name: Heart of the Tribe
nodes.summary: Ngakanu's sacred core with the Meeting House (Words of Akoya) and the Act 4 final boss arena where Tavakai is fought.
sources: map: Heart of the Tribe, Act Boss Tavakai

nodes.name: Highgate
nodes.summary: Mountain region where Veruso buried the virtue gems ('Tears of Maji'), where slaves mined them under Chitus, where Malachai placed the Rapture Device and the Beast lies beneath, and where a Maraketh tribe lives in PoE1.
sources: 'Reign of Tarcus Veruso', 'Slave trade', 'Reign of Voll'

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh-held mining settlement north of Sarn, Act 4 town.
Mining town built over the Beast's corpse; Act 9 town whose waters run red with the Beast's blood. Maraketh Irasha, Tasuni and relic hunters Petarus and Vanja live here.

nodes.name: Holten
nodes.summary: Ezomyte holding of Thane Wulfric and Lady Elswyth, behind the Blackwood; centre of the Curse of Holten.
sources: Enter Holten / Defeat the Thane and Lady

nodes.name: Hunting Grounds
nodes.summary: Act 1 area beyond the clan graves that Una directs the Exile through toward Ogham Village.

nodes.name: Infested Barrens
nodes.summary: Area where the stone altar needs a large Soul Core to open the Matlan Waterways.

nodes.name: Isle of Kin
nodes.summary: Act 4 island with the Volcanic Warrens; boss The Blind Beast and Krutog, Lord of Kin. Doomed Mine holds Niko's Feverish Writings.

nodes.name: Isles of Skothe
nodes.summary: Landmass west of Sarn named with Ezomyr as the origin of the Ezomytes.

nodes.name: Jiquani's Machinarium
nodes.summary: Unlooted Vaal facility in the Chimeral Wetlands holding a large Soul Core in Jiquani's Sanctum, needed to run the Matlan Waterways.

alt_summaries.summary: Unlooted Vaal facility with a stone door that needs a small Soul Core.

nodes.name: Jiquani's Sanctum
nodes.summary: Deep chamber with generators and the large Soul Core, guarded by Zicoatl.

nodes.name: Kalguur
nodes.summary: Homeland of the Kalguur people in Middengard, a distant continent southeast/east of Wraeclast; not directly accessible but referenced by Expedition and Settlers of Kalguur.

alt_summaries.summary: Homeland of the Kalguurans on the continent Middengard, south-east of Wraeclast; ruled by a mysterious King Cadigan who gives charters to successful outposts.

nodes.name: Kedge Bay and Journey's End
nodes.summary: Fog-covered island whose Karui totems keep Tangmazu (appearing as Freya Hartlin) imprisoned; its fog disrupts Kingsmarch trade.

nodes.name: Keth
nodes.summary: Ancient Maraketh city and trade empire at the meeting of seven rivers, called the 'glory of the world'; ruins form an Act 2 area in PoE2.
sources: Walkthrough 'Use the Desert Map to travel to Keth'

alt_summaries.summary: Buried city where the Water Goddess Halani lies and the Essence of Water is found.

nodes.name: The Khari Bazaar
nodes.summary: Interlude 2 settlement where Risu gives the Clearing the Way quest.
sources: Quest infobox: 'Speak to Risu at the Khari Bazaar'

nodes.name: Khari Crossing
nodes.summary: Desert crossing near the Khari Bazaar in PoE2 Interlude 2; the far end is plagued by Akthi and Anundr.
sources: Quest log: 'Travel to the Khari Crossing' and 'The way is plagued by a great scorpion and a massive sandworm'

nodes.name: Kingsmarch
nodes.summary: Kalguuran harbour town on Ngamakanui, hub of Act 4 where the Exile hires the Aurora May. Founded in PoE1's Settlers of Kalguur; Tujen says they first picked the spot to stash supplies and 'now it's going to be a city'. In the epilogue its ruins are revisited by Dannig and Makoru.
sources: intro + '==NPCs=='; Trivia 'Act 4 town in Path of Exile 2'

alt_summaries.summary: Kalguuran-chartered port and hub town on the Karui coast, reached via Johan in the Karui Shores (Epilogue). Run by the King's Hand under a Charter, it hosts Dannig, Tujen, Rog, Isla, Faustus, Raulf and Sonja. In PoE2 it is the Act 4 town and later lies in ruins in the endgame.

nodes.name: Korathin
nodes.summary: Capital of Trarthus, declared by Ixan Keita in 872 IC and built by his slaves.

nodes.name: Lake of Kalandra
nodes.summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars in primordial Wraeclast where Kalandra is trapped. The league version was a mirror-realm assembled from a Mirrored Tablet and was not added to the core game.
sources: League Mechanic and note on core game

alt_summaries.summary: Boundless lake of basalt pillars that existed when 'nothing but the lake' did; Kalandra is trapped in it. The Kalandra league lets the Exile stage reflected encounters there.

nodes.name: Lioneye's Watch
nodes.summary: Southern Eternal garrison commanded by General Marceus Lioneye, taken by Kaom's Karui in the Purity Rebellion; later the survivors' town in PoE1 Acts 1 and 6.
sources: Lioneye's Watch is the Act 6 town

alt_summaries.summary: Act 1 town of exile survivors on the coast, named after General Marceus Lioneye; conquered by Kaom's Karui in the past.
Coastal refugee town on the Twilight Strand; Act 1 town and, in Part Two, the Act 6 town where Tarkleigh, Bestel, Lilly Roth and Sin await the exile.

nodes.name: Lira Vaal / Atziri's Temple
nodes.summary: Royal temple of Atziri and Vaal capital for much of its history; rebuilt by Xipocado and Doryani as a self-reconstructing marvel. PoE2 Fate of the Vaal league lets players modify its layout.

nodes.name: The Lord's Labyrinth
nodes.summary: A labyrinth built by Emperor Izaro in 1317 IC as a test to choose his successor, opened on the second Galvano of Azmeri. Chitus won it by betraying Weylin, and later sealed Izaro inside. In PoE1 it is the Act 1 quest that leads to the Trials of Ascendancy.
sources: section 'Reign of Izaro' and 'The Lord's Labyrinth'

alt_summaries.summary: Trap-filled maze built by Emperor Izaro in Sarn to pick his successor, opened 1317 IC. Chitus won it; the exile later challenges it to earn ascendancy points.

nodes.name: The Matlan Waterways
nodes.summary: Vaal canal system whose controls, powered by a large Soul Core, drain the lake to reveal Utzaal.

alt_summaries.summary: Ancient canal system whose control mechanism drains the Utzaal lake.

nodes.name: Mawdun Mine
nodes.summary: Abandoned Faridun foundry guarded by Rudja, the Dread Engineer.

nodes.name: Mawdun Quarry
nodes.summary: Faridun camp where the Countess had Jamanra's followers prepare weapons and the Dreadnought.

nodes.name: Middengard
nodes.summary: Distant continent south-east of Wraeclast on which Kalguur lies.

alt_summaries.summary: Distant continent east/southeast of Wraeclast on which Kalguur lies.
Distant continent south-east of Wraeclast, homeland of the Kalguur; ruled by a king named Cadigan; it cannot be directly visited in the games.

nodes.name: The Molten Vault
nodes.summary: Act 3 vault marked by monkey statues of Kamasa, cleared for treasure in the Treasures of Utzaal quest; its boss is Mektul, the Forgemaster.
sources: Lead: 'entrance to the Molten Vault' and '===Enter The Molten Vault===' quest log

nodes.name: Monastery of the Keepers
nodes.summary: Southern Atlas site; hidden chamber houses the Dreamer; Genesis Tree and Grasping Orchid located here.
sources: Visit the Monastery of the Keepers
hidden area in the Monastery of the Keepers
Monastery of the Keepers to grow a Grasping Orchid

alt_summaries.summary: Keepers' sanctuary housing Ailith and the Genesis Tree.
Hub reached by the Horned Skull; home of the Genesis Tree and Ailith.

nodes.name: Mount Kriar and the Cuachic Vault
nodes.summary: Most isolated peak of the Azmeri Ranges; its summit Cuachic Vault holds Doryani's sealed Vaal reserves.

nodes.name: Mount Veruso
nodes.summary: Mountain beneath which virtue gems were discovered by the Vaal, who used them to gain great power.

nodes.name: Mud Burrow
nodes.summary: Act 1 underground burrow reached from Clearfell, home of the Devourer; also the Abyss-linked passage in Cracks in the Earth.
sources: Lead: 'a quest in the act 1 area Mud Burrow'; walkthrough '===Find the Mud Burrow==='

nodes.name: Ngakanu
nodes.summary: Tukohama-tribe settlement under Chieftain Tavakai, reached late in Act 4; a hostile Blood Fever zone after Tavakai's declaration. Kaimana lives here.
sources: Shipping: Exclusive rewards / Table of rewards

alt_summaries.summary: Karui port that Kingsmarch ships can supply; rewards vary (runegrafts at Kalguuran ports, tattoos at Karui ports).

nodes.name: Ngamakanui
nodes.summary: Karui homeland, an archipelago southwest of Lioneye's Watch; to the Karui the name (Nga + Makanui, 'the Karui Way') denotes anywhere the Karui roam. Explorable in PoE2 Act 4, where it is overrun by the Flesh Scourge (speculative per wiki).
sources: [5:33] Kahuturoa: 'Ngamakanui isn't a place, not really.'

alt_summaries.summary: Karui homeland archipelago, seat of Kaom and Hyrri; where Voll sought Kaom's help.
Karui homeland archipelago.

The Karui 'archipelago': per Kahuturoa, not a fixed place but wherever the Karui bring their Way ('Makanui is our Way'); the Karui deliberately keep its location from the Vaal. Act 4 is set among its islands around Kingsmarch.
Karui archipelago where the weapon pieces lie.

nodes.name: Ogham
nodes.summary: Forest region where the PoE2 campaign opens; Count Geonor rules it from Ogham Manor and the Ezomytes live under his terror.

alt_summaries.summary: Ezomyte village and Act 1 seat of Count Geonor; in Interlude 1 again besieged by the darkness from neighbouring Holten.

nodes.name: Ogham Farmlands
nodes.summary: Act 1 farmland area near Ogham Village where Una's family hut, and her lute, are found.
sources: Tips: 'Una's family hut is south and slightly east of the waypoint'; walkthrough '===Search for Una's Lute==='

nodes.name: Ogham Manor
nodes.summary: Count Geonor's seat in Act 1; the Beast seed was caged in its foundations and fed by hangings.

alt_summaries.summary: Count Geonor's manor; Count Geonor is the Act 1 act boss (Progression table: area level 15, last area).

nodes.name: Ogham Village
nodes.summary: Act 1 village where the Executioner is found and the Seed of Corruption is sought.
sources: Walkthrough 'Find the entrance to the Village'

nodes.name: Oriath
nodes.summary: Island off the south-east of Wraeclast, founded by Innocence's banished followers and ruled by the Templar theocracy from Theopolis. Unaffected by the Cataclysm, it served as the Empire's successor; destroyed in the Atlas storyline of PoE1 and revisited in PoE2 Act 4.

alt_summaries.summary: A small island off Wraeclast's south-east coast, founded by followers of Innocence. Unaffected by the Cataclysm, it became the successor of the Eternal Empire and a Templar theocracy.
Island Theocracy ruled by the Templar.
Capital of the Templar Theocracy; fallen to Kitava's cultists, revisited in Act 10 and rebuilt in the Epilogue.

Former Templar capital destroyed by Sirus in PoE1; PoE2 outsiders think it was abandoned 20 years ago, but the Twilight Order secretly rebuilt its heart and keeps the Beast here (Kanu, Act 4). Setting of the unreleased Act 5.

nodes.name: Path of Mourning
nodes.summary: Route through Deshar that leads the Exile to the Faridun at the Spires.
sources: Quest log 'Travel through the Path of Mourning'

nodes.name: The Patriarch and Matriarch Halls
nodes.summary: Two Precursor halls visited in Legacy of the Precursors; the Exile defeats Phyx, Sentinel of the Spark, and Phya, Sentinel of the Cradle, to recover the Origin Spark and Origin Cradle.
sources: quest log (hidden comment block) steps 112-128: 'Travel to the Patriarch Halls', 'Defeat Phyx, Sentinel of the Spark', 'Defeat Phya, Sentinel of the Cradle'

nodes.name: Phrecia (imperial heartlands)
nodes.summary: Imperial heartlands of the Eternal Empire named in honour of General Alano Phrecia after he drove away a pervasive darkness; contains Phrecia Cathedral (modern Fellshrine Ruins).

nodes.name: Phrecia Cathedral
nodes.summary: Cathedral seat of Archbishop Geofri in the Phrecian heartlands (today the Fellshrine Ruins); Geofri was killed here by Maligaro.

nodes.name: Plunder's Point
nodes.summary: Island unlocked via the Torn Map Pieces of The Runeseeker; abandoned Kalguuran post (Cadigan the Wise's notes) and an Expedition encounter.

nodes.name: Precursor Shrine
nodes.summary: Underground shrine built around a mirror by the 'oldest of men' (probably primeval/precursor); Uhtred hid here and the Kalguuran survivors tried to reach it. No link to Kalandra's mirror is proven.

nodes.name: Precursor Towers
nodes.summary: Precursor Tower system met on the PoE2 Atlas, apparently built for terraforming Wraeclast (per Doryani's research quoted on the History page). In Legacy of the Precursors, activating a Precursor Beacon makes a Precursor Fortress rise from the ground; the Ziggurat sits over ancient 'leylines'.
sources: flavour: 'they sought to master this world'
Activate the Precursor Beacon: 'the Precursor Fortress will rise from the ground'; Doryani on leylines

nodes.name: Qimah
nodes.summary: Maraketh city where the Gifting of Water is held; Qimah Reservoir is Azmadi's arena.

nodes.name: The Red Vale
nodes.summary: Act 1 vale of battle debris where three Obelisks of Rust hold Runes of Power.

nodes.name: The Riverbank
nodes.summary: Act 1 starting area where the Exile washes up after escaping execution; the Bloated Miller is the area boss and the Reaching Clearfell quest starts here.
sources: Act 1 intro and Progression table (The Riverbank, boss: The Bloated Miller)
quest 'Reaching Clearfell' is a quest in the act 1 area The Riverbank

nodes.name: Ruins of Kingsmarch
nodes.summary: Devastated Kingsmarch, hub of the Expedition storyline.

nodes.name: Sandswept Marsh
nodes.summary: Marsh crossed in search of the Ziggurat that marks the sunken city.

nodes.name: Sarn
nodes.summary: Capital of the Eternal Empire, founded by Veruso on the site of Azala Vaal. Burned during the Night of a Thousand Ribbons, rebuilt, besieged by Voll in 1334 IC and fallen within an hour of the Cataclysm. The Act 8 city of the exile.

alt_summaries.summary: Ruined Eternal Empire capital.
Eternal Empire capital founded on the ruins of Azala Vaal.

nodes.name: Sceptre of God
nodes.summary: Imperial palace tower of Sarn where Chitus, Malachai and Dialla held court (concubines kept there); the exile kills Dominus atop it in Act 3.

alt_summaries.summary: Tower in Sarn where Dominus's laboratory stands at the summit.

nodes.name: Shrike Island
nodes.summary: Act 4 island where Karui youths take the Test of Might; boss Scourge of the Skies.

nodes.name: Solaris Temple
nodes.summary: Sarn temple where Malachai built the Rapture Device over more than a year; the exile meets Dialla on Level 2 in Act 3.
sources: Maramoa on The Dawn and the Sun Orb

alt_summaries.summary: Temple in north-east Sarn where Lady Dialla is found.
Sarn temple holding the Sun Orb, guarded by the exile 'Dawn'.

nodes.name: Temple of Chaos
nodes.summary: Vaal temple near the outskirts of Utzaal where commoners could attempt the Trials of Chaos to become high priests; in PoE2 Act 3, off the Chimeral Wetlands.
sources: paragraph on the Temple of Chaos

alt_summaries.summary: Temple of Vaal priests dedicated to Chaos on the outskirts of Utzaal; site of the PoE2 Trial of Chaos.

nodes.name: Temple of Kopec
nodes.summary: Sealed Vaal sun-god temple beneath the Ziggurat Encampment, guarded by Ketzuli; houses the time gateway used to travel to Utzaal's past.
sources: Quest log 'Enter the Temple of Kopec'

alt_summaries.summary: Temple of the Sun God beneath the treasure-hunter camp, where Ketzuli is defeated and the gateway is found.

nodes.name: The Abyss (place)
nodes.summary: Underground realm reached through Abyss pits; Abyssal Depths.

nodes.name: The Black Cathedral
nodes.summary: Level-80 area off the Well of Souls entered only with Kulemak's Invitation; site of the Kulemak encounter.
sources: area table: The Black Cathedral 80 - Kulemak's Invitation

nodes.name: The Breach (realm)
nodes.summary: Parallel realm opened by breaches in which Breachlords hold domains; see concept_breach.
sources: lead: breaches open a parallel realm containing otherworldly monsters

nodes.name: The Burning Monolith
nodes.summary: Site where the Arbiter of Ash is fought; in 0.1-0.4 a door on the Atlas opened by three Crisis Fragments, in 0.5 moved inside the Precursor Fortress.
sources: Three Crisis Fragments, one from each Citadel, open the Burning Monolith

alt_summaries.summary: Endgame structure where the Arbiter of Ash is fought and the Fourth Edict is investigated, with the Origin Tower beyond it.

nodes.name: The Cradle
nodes.summary: Mirror-portal realm near the Beast where Atziri, the Fell Serpent is fought in PoE2.

nodes.name: The Dreadnought
nodes.summary: Faridun war caravan carrying the Beast across the Vastiri; the Act 2 boss is fought on it.

nodes.name: The Excavation
nodes.summary: Twilight Order dig site on Arastas, boss Benedictus; leads to the Excavated Site whose murals depict the Weapon and the Beast and where the Weapon is reforged.
sources: Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru 'These murals... appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast'

nodes.name: The Grelwood
nodes.summary: Act 1 forest containing the Tree of Souls that binds the Hooded One.

nodes.name: The Origin Tower
nodes.summary: Precursor tower reached via the Waygate in the Epilogue; the Exile places the Origin Core at the top, where Tecrod intervenes and the Arbiter of Divinity is fought.
sources: area: the Burning Monolith, the Origin Tower

alt_summaries.summary: Tower at the Fortress core where the Origin Core is placed and the Arbiter of Divinity is fought.

nodes.name: The Precursor Fortress
nodes.summary: Vast Precursor structure that rises from the ground when the first Precursor Beacon is activated (0.5); contains the Ancient/Western/Eastern Gateways, Enigma Chambers, the Burning Monolith, the Halls and the Origin Tower. Official 0.5.0 notes: 'The Cataclysm of the Beast has invoked an ancient protocol'; players seek keys to reach and disarm ancient Precursor weapons.
sources: Activate the Precursor Beacon: Fortress will rise from the ground
Origins of Divinity: ancient protocol; obtain keys to reach the Precursor weapons and disarm them

nodes.name: Slums and Grand Arena (Oriath)
nodes.summary: Named on the PoE2 wiki as the progression areas of Act 5; datamined further areas: Gardens, Den of Pleasure, Pantheon of the Forsaken Gods. Unreleased.

nodes.name: Theopolis
nodes.summary: Capital city of the Theocracy of Oriath; site of the Oriath academy where Valdo worked and of the Templar Laboratory.
sources: Memory of Wonder: 'a map of Theopolis'

alt_summaries.summary: Capital of Oriath and seat of the High Templar; home of the Grand Arena where Daresso fought.

nodes.name: The Titan Grotto
nodes.summary: Grotto beneath the Valley of the Titans where Zalmarath guards the Flame Ruby.
sources: Walkthrough 'Find a way into the Titan Grotto'

nodes.name: Traitor's Passage
nodes.summary: Hidden tunnel leading to the top of the Halani Gates, where Balbala is sealed as a Djinn.

nodes.name: Trarthus
nodes.summary: Region southwest of Wraeclast and west of the Karui archipelago; capital Korathin; a brutal slave-and-killer culture ruled by four Great Houses, once the Eternal Empire's dumping ground for exiles.

alt_summaries.summary: Land south-west of Wraeclast used by the Empire as an exile colony; rebelled in 870 IC.

nodes.name: Utzaal
nodes.summary: Vaal city, centre of Doryani's research, drowned by its own waterways at the Cataclysm to spite looters. PoE2 Act 3 setting: the Exile drains the Sunken City, then travels to its living past.
sources: Quest logs 'Speak to the Hooded One' / 'Enter Utzaal in the past'

alt_summaries.summary: Sunken Vaal city in the jungles of Act 3; the Hooded One sends the Exile to Utzaal to seek knowledge of the Beast. Its past version is reached through a time gateway.

nodes.name: Vaal Ruins (PoE2)
nodes.summary: Endgame hub in PoE2 east/north-east of the Atlas start with a waypoint and Temple Console for Atziri's Temple.

nodes.name: Vastiri (Plains / Desert)
nodes.summary: Region bordering Phaaryl, Lira Vaal and Sarn, home of the Maraketh; once a lush land of forests and seven rivers around Keth, it became a desert over thousands of years after the Beast silenced the gods.

alt_summaries.summary: Maraketh desert east of Highgate with the oasis shielded by Shakari's sandstorm.

nodes.name: The Venom Crypts
nodes.summary: Act 3 crypt area containing the Den of the Serpent Priestess, where the Corpse-snake Venom quest item is found.
sources: Quest lead: 'explore the area to find the landmark Den of the Serpent Priestess'

nodes.name: The Well of Souls
nodes.summary: Wellspring of necromancy that collects all souls; Kulemak's seat. In PoE2 reached via the Lightless Passage from Mastodon Badlands in Act 2; later the Abyss hub.

alt_summaries.summary: Source of necromantic power that collects all souls; hub area in PoE2 Abyss content.

nodes.name: Whakapanu Island
nodes.summary: Lush Act 4 island whose Karui carvings tell of settlers repeatedly vanishing into the Singing Caverns, where the Siren Diamora hunts; boss Great White One.

nodes.name: The Withered Willow
nodes.summary: Delirium hub on the 0.5 Atlas, south-west of the starting point.

nodes.name: Wraeclast
nodes.summary: The continent on which the Exile's story takes place; PoE2 is set on (and expands) Wraeclast, while Oriath is another continent seen in PoE1.

alt_summaries.summary: The continent where the Exile is sent. It was the site of the Precursor, Primeval, Vaal and Eternal Empire civilisations, and the Cataclysm's effects were mostly confined to its landmass.
Forsaken continent where exiles are sent.
Continent of the Path of Exile setting.

nodes.name: Ziggurat Encampment
nodes.summary: Treasure hunter camp built atop a ziggurat in a lake; unknowingly sits on the time gateway. Town hub of PoE2 Act 3.

alt_summaries.summary: Treasure-hunter camp on a ziggurat in the lake of Utzaal; Act 3 hub with Alva, Oswald, and Servi.

nodes.name: Ziggurat Refuge
nodes.summary: Where the Exile unintentionally ends up instead of Oriath; Doryani's Ziggurat above Precursor leylines holds the Waygate/Map Device.
sources: Take a Waystone from Doryani in The Ziggurat Refuge

alt_summaries.summary: Endgame hub (the wiki also calls it the Ziggurat Encampment) where Doryani keeps the Waygate; the Ziggurat stands over what his ancestors called leylines. Quest Siege of Oriath ends with the Exile arriving here.

nodes.name: Ancient Etchings (Kalandra)
nodes.summary: Series of Ancient Etchings in the Lake of Kalandra written by Kalandra herself, recounting her entrapment, scorn for gods (Etching V: a conversation with someone implied to be Sin), and the Order of the Djinn's failed rescue (Etching VI).
sources: Prehistory > The Lake of Kalandra footnotes
Ancient Etchings entry (found throughout the Lake)

alt_summaries.summary: Series of etchings in the Lake of Kalandra written by Kalandra: her entry, view of gods as 'thieves of virtue', a conversation with a 'little thief' (Sin), the Order of the Djinn's abandoned promise, and a new escape plan.

nodes.name: The First Edict
nodes.summary: Unexplained so far. Tecrod, hunting for the Edicts, is destroyed by the Arbiter of Divinity with 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'; on completing the Epilogue quest Legacy of the Precursors the log reads 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.' Its contents are not described in sources read; 'ordain' implies it is something that can be enacted or activated, and the Origin Tower / Origin Core are the setting.
sources: Lore: 'Your kind shall never ordain the First Edict!'
Quest Complete: 'Wraeclast is now safe from the threat of the First Edict.'

nodes.name: The Fourth Edict
nodes.summary: Mystery edict. In Legacy of the Precursors (0.5.0) the quest-log step 'Investigate the Fourth Edict' follows the defeat of the Arbiter of Ash; its contents are not revealed in the verified sources.
sources: The Great Fire: 'likely caused by the Fourth Edict, a contingency created by the Precursors to purge Wraeclast in flames'
quote 'The Fourth Edict beckons' (flaming orb attack) - reported via search result, unverified locally
fan answer: fourth edict = flame seed (speculation)

nodes.name: The Second Edict
nodes.summary: Never shown directly. Only Doryani's speculation, after the Third Edict is revealed: 'Perhaps it follows that the Seed was the instrument of a Second Edict... Why would any civilisation intentionally create the Seed of Corruption?'
sources: Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani 'Perhaps it follows that the Seed was the instrument of a Second Edict...'

nodes.name: The Third Edict
nodes.summary: Precursor edict whose instrument is the Weapon. After the Hooded One reforges it, the inscription reads 'The instrument of the Third Edict'; the Weapon was 'designed for the sole purpose of cleansing Corruption... and destroying the Beast'. Revealed in Act 4 (0.3.0, whose update bears the name 'The Third Edict'). The Hooded One's wording ('that third mural') implies the edicts are murals he had seen in the Excavated Site.
sources: Return to Kingsmarch: Hooded One 'It is the Weapon I saw in that third mural. The forging revealed an inscription. The symbols declare it The instrument of the Third Edict.'
Version history 0.3.0: 'The instrument of the Third Edict. Journey to Kingsmarch...'

nodes.name: Emperor's Warning
nodes.summary: Notice at The Prisoner's arena: 'By the order of Emperor Izaro... The prisoner within is beyond death.' signed Emperor Chitus Perandus.

nodes.name: Feverish Writings (Niko)
nodes.summary: Letter by Niko ('Your master, Niko') in the Doomed Mine on the Isle of Kin, urging miners to gather sulphite while a blind beast whispers in the dark. Continues PoE1's Niko (Delve) into PoE2.

nodes.name: Count Geonor's Edicts (Ogham decrees)
nodes.summary: Notices posted across Ogham by Count Geonor declaring all crimes punishable by hanging, bodies thrown into a pit beneath his manor; a 'notice of criminality' is found near Clearfell. Not Precursor edicts; the executions fed the Beast seed/creature in the manor cage.
sources: [0:25]-[0:41] 'The count's edicts posted throughout the island declared that all crimes were now punishable by hanging'; [4:25]-[4:36]

nodes.name: Geonor's Journal
nodes.summary: Environmental lore in Ogham Manor: Geonor writes that Oriana 'assures me, we can right some of the wrongs of the past' and promises a way forward for Ogham, showing how the Countess recruited him.

nodes.name: Letters from Chitus
nodes.summary: Three letters from Chitus to Cadiro (1316-1318 IC) planning to win Izaro's Labyrinth. Released as physical GGG merchandise.

nodes.name: Letters of Exile
nodes.summary: Environmental lore object in Lioneye's Watch: court papers nailed to stakes that give the sentences of named exiles (1597-1599 IC) in the formula 'You are hereby Exiled to Wraeclast where, it is hoped, you shall come to repent your Sins'. Added in version 0.10.8. Distinct from text_letters_from_chitus (Chitus's letters to Cadiro) and text_vaal_letters (Vaal victims' letters).
sources: intro: 'Letters of Exile is an environmental lore object found in Lioneye's Watch.'; section '==Format==' sentencing formula; version history 0.10.8

nodes.name: The Lord's Labyrinth (gamebook)
nodes.summary: An official GGG gamebook (2019) that retells the Lord's Labyrinth from Weylin's perspective. The PoE Wiki reports repeated inconsistencies with in-game sources, so it is generally not treated as canon.
sources: gamebook forum post, 28 Oct 2019 (cited in History of Wraeclast, 'The Lord's Labyrinth')
section 'The Lord's Labyrinth' (gamebook note: generally not canon)

nodes.name: Lycia's relics
nodes.summary: Forbidden Sanctum relics revealing the Original Sin and Innocence's ascension.

nodes.name: Path of Exile: Origins
nodes.summary: Official comic recounting Victario, the Karui Way, the Chamber of Sins and Chitus' death.

nodes.name: Path of Exile: Origins (comic)
nodes.summary: A four-issue official comic by Grinding Gear Games and Dynamite Entertainment, told from Victario's perspective. Digital issues ran from July 2014 to April 2015; the paperback was published by Dynamite in June 2015. It centres on the Purity Rebellion and events leading up to the Cataclysm.
sources: 'Publication' section (issue table) and intro: written by Edwin McRae and Royal McGraw, illustrated by Carlos Rodriguez

nodes.name: Precursor Edicts
nodes.summary: Vague Precursor murals depicting the Beast (or a precursor of it) and possibly instructions for containing it. The corpus separately says Sin later created the Beast from a Precursor Seed of Corruption; any reading that the Beast predates the gods is interpretation.

nodes.name: The Purity Chronicles
nodes.summary: Six-book chronicle by Garivaldi in the Library of Sarn (Act 3 area) on the Purity Rebellion.

nodes.name: Memory Fragments of the Shaper
nodes.summary: Seven in-game diary entries (Home, Intrigue, Wonder, Dream, Nightmare, Grief, Awakening) in which Valdo describes the golden device, dreams, Zana's capture and resolving to 'forge a world anew'. Partly superseded by the Book of Memories retcon.

nodes.name: Chamber of Innocence stained glass windows
nodes.summary: Templar propaganda in Oriath depicting Innocence as pure and Sin as deceitful twin; later contradicted by Lycia.

nodes.name: Tavakai's Declaration
nodes.summary: In-game note found in Ngakanu: Tavakai declares the 'era of the Mighty', that the last Ngakuramakoi's body will become the new world and that 'The End of Time has come'.

nodes.name: The Ancients (Trinian)
nodes.summary: In-game history by Trinian in the Library of Sarn (PoE1 Act 3), Books 1-5 on Atziri, Zerphi, Doryani, the Azmeri and the Fall.

nodes.name: Architects' notes in Atziri's Temple
nodes.summary: Environmental texts in Atziri's Temple: 'The Perfect Design' (Architect's living-machine temple, expecting Doryani's proxies to try to stop 'Atziri's Ascension'), 'Disloyalty' (an Architect suspects Doryani is moving against the Queen over the Red Communion) and 'The Forever Queen' (Atziri names a critic her personal Architect).

nodes.name: Vaal Letters
nodes.summary: Twelve readable letters by victims and subjects of Atziri's regime, documenting sacrifice and dissent.

nodes.name: Victario's Writings
nodes.summary: Four environmental lore texts in The Library, written as anecdotes and allegory by the poet Victario of Sarn: Kalisa Maas and the Virtue gem that shatters glass; the Blackest Monkey parable; Slaves of Virtue, on shackled workers who mine gems for the Eternal citizens while Malachai abuses them; and A Friend in Need, on the musician Lorenzi who has a gem implanted in his hand.
sources: section headings 'Volume 1: Kalisa Maas', 'Volume 2: The Blackest Monkey', 'Volume 3: Slaves of Virtue' (mentions Malachai and Highgate), 'Volume 4: A Friend in Need' (Lorenzi and Malachai's gem implant); each signed 'Victario of Sarn'

nodes.name: Voll's Confession
nodes.summary: Voll's confession that he trusted the most corrupt of men.

edges.description: The arrival beat takes place in Kingsmarch, where the Exile reaches Doryani.
sources: Talk to Doryani (quest log: 'You have arrived in Kingsmarch')

edges.description: Doryani is present in Kingsmarch on arrival and laments the state of the city.
sources: Talk to Doryani: Doryani: 'This is it? This... is Kingsmarch? Science and civilisation must have never recovered.'

edges.description: The Hooded One is with the Exile and Doryani on arrival and comments on the Kalguurans.
sources: Talk to Doryani: The Hooded One: 'Your time was different, yes, but don't discount the Kalguurans just yet. They have potential.'

edges.description: The charter deal with Alva, Rog and Makoru takes place in Kingsmarch.
sources: Talk to Alva / Take the Boat Charter (Alva, Rog and Makoru all speak in Kingsmarch; Makoru: 'we only operate under the Meridian Free Traders of Kingsmarch')

edges.description: Alva introduces the Exile to Rog, the charter seller.
sources: Talk to Alva: Alva: 'Ah, there you are! This is my contact Rog, a trader with a keen eye for valuable artefacts!'

edges.description: Rog sells the Boat Charter in exchange for Vaal treasure.
sources: Talk to Alva: Rog, the Dealer: 'Kalguuran merchant vessels don't intentionally seek out danger... Take it to her.'

edges.description: Makoru, captain of the Aurora May, is the ship's captain the charter secures.
sources: Talk to Makoru: Makoru: 'Welcome aboard. I'm Makoru. Captain of the Aurora May.'

edges.description: Kanu, first mate of the Aurora May, is part of the crew hired in this beat.
sources: Talk to Makoru: Kanu: 'If you're lookin' for a ship, best speak to the boss, Makoru.'

edges.description: One of the rotating islands where a Weapon piece may be found is Isle of Kin.
sources: Progression: island map and 'Precursor weapon pieces & Matiki locations' table (Isle of Kin, Volcanic Warrens)

edges.description: Shrike Island is one of the rotating islands holding a Weapon piece.
sources: Progression: island map (Shrike Island, Boss: Scourge of the Skies) and piece-location table

edges.description: Whakapanu Island is one of the rotating islands holding a Weapon piece.
sources: Progression: island map (Whakapanu Island, Singing Caverns, Boss: Diamora, Song of Death)

edges.description: Krutog, Lord of Kin is a boss the Exile fights while searching the islands for Weapon pieces.
sources: Progression: island map (Volcanic Warrens, Isle of Kin, Boss: Krutog, Lord of Kin)

edges.description: The Scourge of the Skies is a boss the Exile fights on Shrike Island during the piece search.
sources: Progression: island map (Shrike Island, Boss: Scourge of the Skies)

edges.description: Diamora, Song of Death is a boss the Exile fights in Singing Caverns during the piece search.
sources: Progression: island map (Singing Caverns, Whakapanu Island, Boss: Diamora, Song of Death)

edges.description: The Prisoner is a boss in Solitary Confinement, reached while searching for Weapon pieces; that area is not one of the three listed occurs_in locations.
sources: Progression: island map (Solitary Confinement, Abandoned Prison, Boss: The Prisoner)

edges.description: Makoru's ship carries the Exile between the islands during the piece search.
sources: Explore the Islands: 'You have obtained a weapon piece. Speak to Makoru to travel to a new island.'

edges.description: Doryani is present and works to translate the Precursor script the Hooded One recognises.
sources: Witness The Hooded One: Doryani: 'The first example of Precursor writing I've ever seen!'

edges.description: The Utopia quest starts with Missionary Lorandis in Kingsmarch.
sources: Quest description: 'It is begun by speaking with Missionary Lorandis in Kingsmarch'

edges.description: The oath to the Saviour and the offer of Utopia both happen on Arastas.
sources: Quest description: 'encourages you to journey to Arastas take an oath to The Saviour'

edges.description: Missionary Lorandis sends the Exile to Arastas to swear the oath.
sources: Quest description: Missionary Lorandis begins the quest in Kingsmarch and sends the Exile to Arastas

edges.description: Servitor Marius offers the Exile membership in Utopia, and the refusal completes the quest.
sources: Quest description: 'He proposes to join their Utopia or donate to their cause'; completion 'Speak with Servitor Marius'

edges.description: The fight against Torvian takes place on Arastas.
sources: Progression: island map (Arastas, Boss: Torvian, Hand of the Saviour)

edges.description: The fight against Benedictus takes place in the Excavation.
sources: Progression: island map (The Excavation, Boss: Benedictus, First Herald of Utopia)

edges.description: The Countess leaves Benedictus to hold the Exile and retreats.
sources: Confront Kanu and the First Herald: The Countess: 'First Herald... deal with them.'

edges.description: Kanu begs to be taken along and reveals the Beast is in Oriath.
sources: Defeat Benedictus: Kanu: 'Please, please, please! Take me with you, please!'

edges.description: Tavakai strikes Kanu down after Kanu's confession.
sources: Defeat Benedictus: Tavukai: 'Hyaaahhh!' ... 'Let the ancestors judge him.'

edges.description: Makoru witnesses Kanu's treachery during the Benedictus fight.
The reforging and seizure take place in the Excavated Site, which is within the Excavation.
sources: Enter the Excavated Site: Makoru: 'These murals... They appear to depict the Weapon... and the Beast.' (wiki names 'Excavated Site'; treated as the Excavation)

edges.description: Tavakai takes the reforged Weapon for the Karui.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon: Tavakai: 'Taking what is rightfully ours. The Karui will now be stronger than ever before!'

edges.description: Makoru is taken along by Tavakai when he flees.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon: 'Tavakai flees, taking Makoru with him.'

edges.description: The Hooded One performs the reforging and then warns of the Weapon's Corruption.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon: The Hooded One: 'This will take most of my strength... Stand back.'

edges.description: The inscription is read back in Kingsmarch.
sources: Return to Kingsmarch: The Hooded One: 'There is no doubt now in my mind... The symbols declare it The instrument of the Third Edict.'

edges.description: The Weapon is reforged in the Excavated Site before the inscription is read in Kingsmarch.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon (after 'Enter the Excavated Site'): The Hooded One: 'you've done well... Stand back.' (wiki names 'Excavated Site'; treated as the Excavation)

edges.description: Doryani reacts to the inscription and asks about the Edicts.
sources: Return to Kingsmarch: Doryani: 'The Third Edict? What is the meaning... of these Edicts?'

edges.description: Makoru is present for the reforging and seizure.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon: Makoru: 'You fool! They need the Weapon! The world is at stake!'

edges.description: Tavakai is present for the reforging and seizes the Weapon.
sources: Witness the Hooded One reforge the Weapon: Tavakai: 'Behold! The might of the Karui!'

edges.description: Tavakai's three-phase fight takes place at the Heart of the Tribe.
sources: Progression: island map (Heart of the Tribe, Act Boss: Tavakai, the Chieftain)

edges.description: The Heart of the Tribe lies within the Ngakanu area.
sources: Progression: island map (Ngakanu, with Heart of the Tribe below it)

edges.description: Tavakai is the boss the Exile defeats in this beat.
sources: Defeat Tavakai: Tavakai: 'I must be stronger... For the Karui!'; Phase 3: 'The power of the Ancestors is mine!'
